article:
# Modulating Plasma Metal Ion Concentrations as a Cardiovascular Strategy: Evidence for Supplementation and Chelation

## 1. Introduction

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and considerable research has examined whether modifying the body's metal ion status—either by supplementing deficient essential minerals or by removing toxic heavy metals—could prevent or treat CVD. This report synthesizes clinical evidence across three intervention categories: magnesium supplementation, selenium and zinc supplementation, and chelation therapy for toxic metal removal. The central question is whether these approaches constitute feasible, evidence-based preventive or therapeutic strategies, or whether their promise remains unsubstantiated.

## 2. Biological Rationale: Metal Ions and Cardiovascular Health

Two distinct lines of evidence motivate metal-modulating interventions. First, magnesium (Mg²⁺) depletion is common—estimated in more than 25% of the U.S. population—and contributes to hypertension through effects on sympathetic tone, vascular tone, and catecholamine release. Magnesium modulates N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and N-type calcium channels, influencing sympathetic nerve activity, and alters L-type calcium channel-mediated vascular contractility ([Frontiers in Physiology, 2024](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2024.1363975/full)). Low magnesium states may promote myocardial fibrosis, left ventricular hypertrophy, and dysfunction, providing a mechanistic pathway to heart failure in patients with diabetes (Cheng et al., 2025, [JAHA](https://doi.org/10.1161/JAHA.124.038870)).

Second, accumulation of biologically active toxic metals such as lead and cadmium is an established cardiovascular risk factor. Epidemiological data link higher body burdens of these metals to atherosclerotic CVD, and a 2016 review proposed that combining this evidence with chelation trial results could identify new modifiable risk factors ([Lamas et al., 2016, Johns Hopkins](https://pure.johnshopkins.edu/en/publications/heavy-metals-cardiovascular-disease-and-the-unexpected-benefits-o)). These two pathways—essential mineral repletion and toxic metal removal—frame the clinical interventions examined below.

## 3. Magnesium Supplementation

### 3.1 Blood Pressure Effects

Magnesium supplementation has been studied extensively for blood pressure (BP) reduction. A meta-analysis of 34 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (2,028 participants) found that approximately 300 mg/day over about 3 months reduced systolic BP by 2.00 mmHg and diastolic BP by 1.78 mmHg ([Zhang et al. via Power, 2022](https://www.withpower.com/trial/phase-systolic-murmurs-2023-9f658)). A 2024 review confirms this magnitude, reporting a 2 mmHg systolic reduction with a mean dose of 368 mg/day ([Frontiers in Physiology, 2024](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2024.1363975/full)).

Earlier evidence was less favorable. A 2002 meta-analysis of 20 randomized trials (1,220 participants) found only a small, non-significant overall BP reduction (−0.6 mmHg systolic, −0.8 mmHg diastolic), but detected a significant dose-dependent effect: each 10 mmol/day increase in magnesium dose was associated with a 4.3 mmHg systolic reduction (P < .001) ([Jee et al., 2002, Johns Hopkins](https://pure.johnshopkins.edu/en/publications/the-effect-of-magnesium-supplementation-on-blood-pressure-a-meta--3)). This suggests that earlier mixed results reflected insufficient doses and heterogeneous populations.

The response to magnesium is strongly influenced by hypertension status and medication use. A targeted meta-analysis of seven studies in 135 hypertensive patients on antihypertensive medication reported substantial reductions of −18.7 mmHg systolic and −10.9 mmHg diastolic ([Rosanoff & Plesset, 2020, via Power](https://www.withpower.com/trial/phase-1-2019-a4271)). Conversely, controlled hypertensives and normotensive individuals generally experience no BP reduction, even at high doses. Uncontrolled hypertensives may respond to doses as low as 240 mg/day, while untreated hypertensives require doses above 600 mg/day ([Rosanoff et al., 2023, via Power](https://www.withpower.com/trial/phase-systolic-murmurs-2023-9f658)). In individuals with insulin resistance, prediabetes, or noncommunicable diseases, a meta-analysis of 11 RCTs found reductions of 4.18 mmHg systolic and 2.27 mmHg diastolic ([Dibaba et al., 2017](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2024.1363975/full)).

### 3.2 Post-Myocardial Infarction and Heart Failure Outcomes

Observational evidence links higher dietary magnesium intake with improved outcomes after myocardial infarction. In the Alpha Omega Cohort of 4,365 Dutch post-MI patients, those with intakes above 320 mg/day had a 28% lower risk of cardiovascular death than those below 283 mg/day, with a stronger association in patients taking diuretics ([SuperSmart, 2022](https://www.supersmart.com/en/blog/cardiovascular/magnesium-heart-health-the-latest-scientific-findings-s883)).

A 2025 target trial emulation study in 94,239 U.S. veterans with diabetes found that nonprescription magnesium supplement use was associated with reduced risk of incident heart failure (HR 0.94; 95% CI 0.89–0.99) and major adverse cardiac events including MI, stroke, HF hospitalization, or death (HR 0.94; 95% CI 0.90–0.97). The authors emphasized that these observational findings require confirmation in randomized controlled trials (Cheng et al., 2025, [JAHA](https://doi.org/10.1161/JAHA.124.038870)).

### 3.3 Clinical Interpretation of Magnesium Evidence

The magnesium evidence is the most robust among the interventions examined. The effect on BP is modest in unselected populations but clinically meaningful in hypertensive patients, particularly those on antihypertensive medication. Importantly, magnesium has a favorable safety profile; recent analyses suggest doses up to 1,200 mg/day can be consumed without major gastrointestinal adverse events, and the current tolerable upper intake level of 350 mg/day has been questioned as overly restrictive ([Costello et al., 2023, via Power](https://www.withpower.com/trial/phase-systolic-murmurs-2023-9f658)). The convergence of BP trials, dose-response data, post-MI cohort evidence, and mechanistic plausibility supports magnesium repletion as a reasonable adjunctive strategy—though its absolute BP effect is small relative to standard pharmacotherapy.

## 4. Selenium and Zinc Supplementation

### 4.1 Selenium and Coenzyme Q10

Selenium is a trace element with antioxidant properties via selenoproteins, including thioredoxin reductase, which interacts with coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) in a metabolic pathway converting ubiquinone to its active form. The KiSel-10 trial, a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study of 443 elderly Swedish citizens, tested 200 µg/day selenium combined with 200 mg/day CoQ10 over four years. At 12-year follow-up, cardiovascular mortality was significantly lower in the active treatment group (28.1% vs. 38.7%; HR 0.59; 95% CI 0.42–0.81; P = 0.001), with benefit persisting across subgroups including diabetics and those with hypertension or ischemic heart disease ([Natural Health Research, 2018](https://naturalhealthresearch.org/reduced-risk-of-cardiovascular-death-twelve-years-after-selenium-and-coenzyme-q10-supplementation)).

However, this trial combined two agents, making it impossible to isolate selenium's contribution. A scientific review of micronutrients concluded that evidence for selenium supplementation alone is insufficient and inconsistent; some studies indicate a risk of toxicity, and routine supplementation for cardiovascular prevention is not supported by current data ([Frontiers in Physiology, 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2021.742425/full)). Selenium status follows a U-shaped relationship with health: both deficiency and excess confer risk. Its narrow therapeutic window argues against indiscriminate use, though the KiSel-10 results in a low-selenium European population remain hypothesis-generating and warrant replication.

### 4.2 Zinc

Zinc supplementation evidence is weaker still. Although some studies report improvements in lipid profiles and blood glucose, a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials found no positive effect on cardiovascular health outcomes. Notably, some studies report an association between higher zinc intake and increased total and cancer mortality ([Frontiers in Physiology, 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2021.742425/full)). The review concluded that evidence is insufficient to rationalize zinc supplementation for cardiovascular benefit, and that more consistent experimental data are needed.

## 5. Chelation Therapy for Toxic Metal Removal

### 5.1 The TACT Trial

The hypothesis that removing toxic metals could treat CVD culminated in the Trial to Assess Chelation Therapy (TACT), which randomized 1,708 post-myocardial infarction patients to 40 intravenous infusions of disodium EDTA or placebo. Overall, chelation produced a modest reduction in recurrent cardiac events. The most striking finding was in the 633 diabetic patients: a 41% decrease in major adverse cardiac events over five years, a 43% reduction in relative risk of death, and an approximately 50% reduction in recurrent myocardial infarction ([Interventional News, 2019](https://interventionalnews.com/chelation-therapy-diabetes-cli)). Analysis of the diabetic subgroup showed primary endpoint rates of 25% vs. 38% (P < 0.001) and all-cause mortality of 10% vs. 16% (P = 0.011).

These results, combined with epidemiological evidence linking lead and cadmium to atherosclerotic CVD, suggested that chelation might identify a modifiable risk factor. However, the trial had substantial limitations, including high dropout rates (17% withdrew consent) and the contested nature of the therapy's proposed mechanisms.

### 5.2 The TACT2 Trial

TACT2 was designed to definitively replicate the diabetic subgroup benefit. This NIH-funded, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 959 participants with diabetes and prior MI across 88 U.S. and Canadian sites, randomizing them to 40 weekly infusions of EDTA-based chelation or placebo. The primary composite endpoint—all-cause death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina—occurred in 35.6% of the chelation group versus 35.7% of the placebo group (HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.76–1.16; P = 0.53). The 5-year cumulative incidence was 45.8% vs. 46.5% ([Lamas et al., 2024, JAMA via Duke Scholars](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1642443); [ACC, 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/clinical-trials/2024/04/05/04/40/tact2)).

Critically, TACT2 confirmed that chelation effectively reduced blood lead levels—from a median of 9.03 µg/L at baseline to 3.46 µg/L at infusion 40 (P < 0.001)—and increased cadmium excretion, yet this metal removal produced no clinical benefit ([NIEHS, 2024](https://www.niehs.nih.gov/news/factor/2024/9/papers/chelation)). The authors noted that contemporary patients were treated with modern therapies including SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists, and that background lead levels have declined since TACT, potentially reducing the achievable treatment effect ([ACC, 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/clinical-trials/2024/04/05/04/40/tact2)).

### 5.3 Broader Evidence and Regulatory Status

A systematic review of EDTA chelation in CVD found that 17 of 24 studies reported improved outcomes, but the evidence was limited by lack of clinical outcomes, heterogeneous infusion methods, small sample sizes, and short follow-up ([Ravalli et al., 2022, Duke Scholars](https://scholars.duke.edu/publication/1512352)). A Cochrane review found no difference between chelation and placebo for all-cause mortality (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.73–1.28), cardiovascular death (RR 1.02), or myocardial infarction (RR 0.81) ([Cochrane review via policy summary](https://employer.myhealthtoolkitex.com/web/public/brands/medicalpolicyhb/external-policies/chelation-therapy-for-off-label-uses)). As of the mid-2020s, chelation therapy remains FDA-approved only for heavy metal poisoning (lead, mercury, copper); its use for CVD and other non-overload conditions remains investigational and controversial, with studies ongoing in 2024–2025 for CVD, Alzheimer's disease, autism, chronic kidney disease, and Parkinson's disease ([EBSCO, 2024](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/chelation-therapy)).

## 6. Comparative Synthesis

The following table summarizes the evidence across intervention categories:

| Intervention | Target | Key evidence | Effect size | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Magnesium supplementation | Essential mineral repletion | Meta-analyses of 34 and 20 RCTs; cohort studies | SBP −2.0 to −4.2 mmHg; −18.7/−10.9 mmHg in medicated hypertensives; HF HR 0.94 | Modest but consistent; strongest in hypertensive/diabetic populations |
| Selenium ± CoQ10 | Antioxidant/selenoprotein support | KiSel-10 RCT (n=443) | CV mortality HR 0.59 at 12 years | Promising single trial; toxicity risk; not replicated |
| Zinc supplementation | Essential mineral repletion | Systematic reviews | No CVD benefit; possible harm at high intake | Not supported |
| EDTA chelation | Toxic metal (lead, cadmium) removal | TACT (n=1,708), TACT2 (n=959), Cochrane review | TACT diabetic subgroup: 41% MACE reduction; TACT2: HR 0.93 (ns) | Not effective in definitive trial; FDA-approved only for metal poisoning |

## 7. Conclusion and Position

The accumulated evidence permits a nuanced but definitive assessment. **Magnesium supplementation is the only metal-modulating intervention with sufficient evidence to support targeted clinical use.** Its BP-lowering effect is modest in unselected individuals but clinically relevant in uncontrolled hypertensives on medication, and observational data suggest cardiovascular mortality and heart failure benefits in post-MI and diabetic populations. Given its safety, low cost, and mechanistic plausibility, magnesium repletion—particularly in patients with hypertension, diabetes, or diuretic use—is a reasonable adjunctive preventive strategy, though it should not replace established pharmacotherapy.

**Selenium supplementation, alone or with CoQ10, is promising but unproven.** The KiSel-10 long-term mortality benefit is striking, but it derives from a single small trial combining two agents in a selenium-deficient European population. Selenium's narrow therapeutic window and toxicity risk preclude routine recommendation.

**Zinc supplementation is not supported by current evidence** and may carry harm at high doses. It should not be recommended for cardiovascular prevention.

**Chelation therapy represents a compelling biological hypothesis that failed its definitive test.** The TACT diabetic subgroup results raised the possibility that removing vasculotoxic metals could reduce cardiovascular events. TACT2, however, demonstrated decisively that despite effectively lowering blood lead and increasing cadmium excretion, chelation did not reduce cardiovascular events in the very population that appeared to benefit most. This outcome suggests that in contemporary, optimally-managed patients, toxic metal removal alone does not translate into clinical benefit—either because metal burdens have declined, because modern pharmacotherapy overwhelms any chelation effect, or because the TACT subgroup findings were partly spurious. Chelation therapy for CVD should remain outside standard clinical practice, restricted to its FDA-approved indication of heavy metal poisoning.

The broader lesson is that modulating metal ion concentrations is biologically plausible but clinically context-dependent. The body's metal status is not a single modifiable target but a complex system in which dose, population, and disease stage determine outcomes. Future research should focus on well-powered trials of magnesium in high-risk populations, and on identifying biomarkers (such as baseline magnesium or lead levels) that could predict differential treatment response. Until then, the most defensible clinical strategy is targeted magnesium repletion—not universal supplementation, and certainly not chelation.

# 市政污水收集处理高效化改革路径研究——从核拨制到“厂网一体、按效付费、智慧调度”的系统方案

## 摘要

当前我国多数城市对市政污水收集处理采用“核拨制”（按处理水量核拨经费），该机制在历史上推动了行业专业化，但日益暴露出“重水量、轻效能”的弊端：清水进厂、外水混入、厂网分离、财政资金低效等问题突出。本文基于武汉、湘潭、长沙、沅江、广州、深圳等地的最新实践，提出政府管理部门可操作的系统性改革方案：以**厂网一体化**打破管理壁垒，以**按效付费**重构激励约束，以**智慧水务平台**实现厂网河联合调度并与雨水排涝协同，同时辅以资产清查、价格动态调整、风险分担等配套机制，从而在降低全生命周期成本的同时实现环境效益与财政绩效的双赢。

## 一、核拨制的制度缺陷与改革必要性

传统“单一水价按量付费”模式下，污水处理服务费仅与处理水量挂钩，与污染物削减效能脱钩。这导致三方面问题：一是**资源浪费**，大量地下水渗流、雨水等“清水”挤占处理能力，形成“清水进厂、低效处理”；二是**财政低效**，政府为无效处理买单；三是**治污导向偏差**，运营企业缺乏维护管网、收集高浓度污水的动力，甚至希望清水稀释以降低成本（[大岳咨询，2026](http://dayue.com/index.php/index/shows?catid=20&id=269)）。同时，“厂网分离”体制下，污水处理厂与管网分属不同责任主体，形成“九龙治水”局面，管网破损、混错接、外水入渗等问题长期得不到系统解决（[搜狐，2026](https://www.sohu.com/a/1025093060_121106908)）。

国家层面已明确改革方向。2023年12月，国家发改委、住建部、生态环境部提出建立与进水污染物浓度、污染物削减量、出水水质、污泥无害化处理效果挂钩的按效付费机制；2024年3月，住建部等5部门进一步要求对污水处理厂和管网联动按效付费（[恒星物联，2025](https://www.starwater-iot.com/newsDetail1615.html)）。这意味着，从“按量付费”转向“按效付费”已成为政策刚需，关键在于如何设计可落地的操作方案。

## 二、厂网一体化：统一责任主体与全链条管控

厂网一体化是将污水处理厂、管网、泵站等纳入统一责任主体（如“水管家”模式），实现从源头收集到末端处理的全链条统筹管控。这是解决厂网分离、权责碎片化的根本性体制安排（[搜狐，2026](https://www.sohu.com/a/1025093060_121106908)）。

### 2.1 武汉“三步走”经验

武汉市自2025年起实施“厂网一体”改革，分三步推进：**调度一体化、运维一体化、建管一体化**，并选取黄陂后湖、黄家湖等试点先行先试（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。具体做法包括：

- **调度一体化**：全市25个污水系统全部制定一体化调度方案，中心城区由市水务局统筹，新城区由各区统筹；搭建“厂网一体”调度系统，引入人工智能与大数据分析，实现管网运行实时监测、异常自动报警（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。
- **运维一体化**：中心城区由市水务局会同区政府选取专业单位委托运营，黄家湖、豹澥、沌口等6个污水系统已实现一体化运维（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。
- **建管一体化**：开展管网资产清查，推进混错接和缺陷整改，同时拓展“水务+光伏”、污泥资源化等绿色产业链（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。

改革成效显著：2025年全市污水处理厂平均进水BOD浓度较“十四五”期初提升30.15%，城市生活污水集中收集率提升至83.65%，管网混错接和缺陷整改快速推进（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。

### 2.2 沅江“水管家”模式

湖南沅江市采用“BOT+TOT”模式，由三峡智慧水管家公司统一运营自来水厂、水质净化厂、排水管网及附属设施，实现“供排一体化”全链条负责。该模式将中心城区厂网一体化运营分为污水厂、市政雨污管网、厂外排水配套设施三个板块，并通过智慧水务平台全方位监控（[搜狐，2026](https://www.sohu.com/a/1025093060_121106908)）。其核心启示是：**只有让一个主体对“源头端—输送端—处理端”整体负责，绩效责任才能精准落地**。

## 三、按效付费：从“买水量”到“买效果”

按效付费的核心是将污水处理服务费与进水污染物浓度、污染物削减量、出水水质、污泥无害化处理效果等关键指标挂钩，倒逼运营企业主动维护管网、收集高浓度污水并高效处理（[搜狐，2026](https://www.sohu.com/a/1025093060_121106908)）。各地探索出三种可操作模式：

### 3.1 武汉：渐进式绩效调节模式

武汉采用“按量付费+绩效调节”的过渡方案，付费公式为：

**F = Q × P × J − W**

其中，Q为付费水量（保底水量为设计规模的60%，雨季超量部分按0.6倍折算），P为基本价格，J为激励系数（月度考核得分/100+0.05），W为违约扣减（[武汉市水务局，2023](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/xxgk/new_zc/new_gfxwj/202312/P020231201394929220477.pdf)）。绩效考核体系在传统出水水质、污泥处理基础上，新增污染物削减量与削减率指标（占20分），并设10分奖惩指标（进水浓度提升、超量削减、节能降耗等）（[大岳咨询，2026](http://dayue.com/index.php/index/shows?catid=20&id=269)）。该模式的优势在于**改革阻力小、企业易接受**，通过“得分—系数—收益”的清晰关联，引导运营方从单一水量保障转向系统效能提升。

### 3.2 湘潭：污染物削减率挂钩模式

湘潭市将运维直接费拆分为固定部分和与加权削减率挂钩的浮动部分，以COD、BOD、氨氮、总氮、总磷五项污染物的实际削减率加权计算付费。实施后，进厂污水BOD浓度同比提升20.8%，首年减少无效处理费用约1300多万元，费用节约率7.6%（[大岳咨询，2026](http://dayue.com/index.php/index/shows?catid=20&id=269)）。该模式直接锚定治污实效，有效规避“清水进厂”的财政浪费。

### 3.3 长沙：分质定价+厂网联动

长沙将污水处理服务费分为建设投资成本、变动运营成本（与进水污染物浓度、水量挂钩）、固定运营成本三部分，并设置“厂网联动”考核，将污水处理厂与管网运营单位的绩效系统性衔接，实现“一荣俱荣、一损俱损”的协同治污（[大岳咨询，2026](http://dayue.com/index.php/index/shows?catid=20&id=269)）。这种模式通过分质定价精准覆盖成本差异，避免“一刀切”定价导致的资源错配。

### 3.4 绩效指标体系设计要点

综合各地实践，一套可操作的按效付费绩效体系应包含：

| 指标类别 | 具体指标 | 建议权重 |
|---------|---------|---------|
| 污水收集效能 | 污水集中收集率、管网完好率、进水BOD/COD浓度达标率 | 20–25分 |
| 污水处理质量 | 出水水质达标率、主要污染物去除率 | 30–35分 |
| 污泥处置效能 | 污泥无害化处置率、含水率达标率 | 15–20分 |
| 设施运行管理 | 设备综合运行率、安全生产、在线监测稳定性 | 15–20分 |
| 鼓励指标 | 节能降耗、再生水利用、应急处置、数字化管理 | 10–20分 |

（[恒星物联，2026](https://www.starwater-iot.com/newsDetail1710.html)）

付费结构可采用“基础服务费+绩效服务费”模式，基础服务费覆盖固定成本和合理收益（原则上不低于运营成本的60%），绩效服务费根据考核得分乘以绩效系数确定（如≥95分系数1.1，<60分系数0并扣减基础费）（[恒星物联，2026](https://www.starwater-iot.com/newsDetail1710.html)）。

## 四、智慧水务与厂网河一体化调度：协同雨水排涝的关键

污水处理系统与雨水排洪排涝并非孤立系统。传统模式下，暴雨时大量雨水涌入污水管网，既冲击污水处理厂，又加剧内涝；旱季则因水量不足导致处理效能低下。智慧水务平台通过“源网站厂河”一体化联调联控，可有效解决这一矛盾。

### 4.1 广州花都：源网站厂河联调联控

广州市花都区构建“源网站厂河”一体化联调联控系统，对8990个排水单元、2809公里管网、174座泵坑、8座污水泵站、4座污水厂实施全要素数字化管理。系统根据降雨强度灵活切换排水模式：**暴雨时优先保障排涝，旱季时提升污水处理效率**，实现“一张网统管、一盘棋调度”（[广州市水务局，2025](http://swj.gz.gov.cn/swyw/gqsw/content/post_10392553.html)）。2024年汛期，新华污水处理系统通过智能调度，防汛响应速度提升30%，COD浓度同比提升16%。

### 4.2 深圳：自适应调度降本增效

深圳环水集团的自适应调度实践显示，通过机器学习智能决策，可实现“晚开泵、早关泵、优先开能耗低的水泵”，配水能耗降低约5%，综合电耗降低约3.5%，人力成本下降35.6%（[深圳市国资委，2024](https://gzw.sz.gov.cn/gkmlpt/content/11/11848/post_11848468.html)）。这证明智慧调度不仅能提升排水安全，还能直接降低运营成本。

### 4.3 内涝预报与应急协同

基于物联网感知设备和AI模型，智慧排水系统可实现分钟级内涝预报与预警，支持灾前预警研判、灾中动态响应、灾后评估优化（[山东瀚臻物联，无日期](https://www.hanzn.com/alibity/cate14a/480.html)）。政府管理部门可将排水管网液位、泵站运行、气象降雨等数据接入统一平台，实现污水系统与排涝系统的联合调度，避免“上游暴雨、下游闲置”的资源错配。

### 4.4 必须正视的集成挑战

智慧水务项目失败的首要原因是**与现有系统和基础设施的集成困难**。数据孤岛、通信协议不兼容（Modbus、PROFIBUS、EtherNet/IP等）、遗留系统限制，导致无法实现全面系统可见性（[Smart Water Magazine，2024](https://smartwatermagazine.com/news/hms-networks/why-smart-water-projects-fail-understanding-integration-challenges)）。因此，政府管理部门在推进智慧水务时，应优先投资于**工业协议转换器、工业网关和无线通信解决方案**，建立可靠的工业连接基础，而非盲目上马大平台。同时，需推动IT标准化和跨部门数据治理，打破水务、环保、住建、应急等部门间的数据壁垒（[SNS Insider，2025](https://www.snsinsider.com/reports/smart-water-management-market-8126)）。

## 五、配套保障与成本控制：实现良性循环

### 5.1 资产清查与建管一体化

政府应组织对存量污水收集处理设施进行全面资产清查，明确权属并登记入账，为后续特许经营和资产盘活奠定基础。武汉已出台《市政生活污水收集设施资产评估工作指引》，推动管网资产确值和盘活（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。通过将管网等存量资产注入专业平台公司，可撬动社会资本参与改造，形成“以资产换资金、以资金促改造”的良性循环。

### 5.2 价格机制与资金保障

污水处理费价格应覆盖成本并合理盈利，建立动态调整机制。武汉明确“原则上污水处理收费标准应当补偿污水处理设施建设运营以及污泥处置成本并合理盈利”，并积极争取中央预算内资金、超长期特别国债支持（[武汉市人民政府，2025](https://www.wuhan.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgk/zfwj/bgtwj/202503/t20250310_2549413.shtml)）。湖南通过政银企平台发布项目库，涉及资金500多亿元，争取超长期特别国债和中央预算内资金138亿元（[湖南省人民政府，2024](https://www.hunan.gov.cn/hnyw/zwdt/202410/t20241015_33475437.html)）。

### 5.3 风险分担与动态调整

按效付费改革中，需防范进水水质大幅波动、工业偷排、极端暴雨等外部不可控因素对运营企业的过度惩罚。建议设置**可变成本月度风险补偿机制**，对进水连续高于基准20%且可变成本同比上涨25%的情况，由财政专项补贴增量成本；同时区分工业突发排污、管网整改、设备故障等不同波动诱因，非企业可控因素不予扣分（[中国大气网，2026](https://www.chndaqi.com/column/1985_2.html)）。此外，应建立第三方监测和成本监审机制，确保数据真实、核算公允。

### 5.4 节能降耗与绿色产业链

污水处理是能源密集型行业，全国城市污水厂吨水平均电耗约0.292度，年用电量超250亿度（[九澧咨询，2025](https://www.hnjlzx.net/h-nd-193.html)）。政府可引导运营企业通过智能精确曝气、精准加药、光伏发电、污泥资源化等方式降低能耗药耗。武汉已在黄家湖、北湖等污水厂建成分布式光伏电站，年减碳效果显著（[武汉市水务局，2026](https://swj.wuhan.gov.cn/tzdt/jcss/202603/t20260326_2745222.html)）。这些措施既能降低运营成本，又能减少财政补贴压力。

## 六、结论与建议

核拨制向高效模式的转变，不是单一工具替换，而是**体制、机制、技术、财政四维联动**的系统工程。基于各地实践，本文提出以下操作性方案：

1. **体制上**：推行厂网一体化，将污水处理厂、管网、泵站纳入统一责任主体，实现“调度、运维、建管”三个一体化。建议以试点先行，如武汉的黄陂后湖、黄家湖模式，形成可复制经验后逐步推广。

2. **机制上**：建立“按效付费”体系，采用“基础服务费+绩效服务费”结构，将付费与污染物收集效能、削减效能、出水水质、污泥处置效果挂钩。对于改革阻力较大的城市，可先采用武汉式“按量付费+绩效调节”渐进过渡，再逐步扩大绩效权重。

3. **技术上**：建设“源网站厂河”一体化智慧调度平台，整合气象、降雨、管网液位、泵站运行、污水厂负荷等数据，实现暴雨时优先排涝、旱季提升处理效率的协同调度。同时，务必重视工业连接层建设，解决协议转换和数据孤岛问题，避免智慧水务项目“有平台无数据”。

4. **财政上**：开展资产清查，盘活存量管网资产；理顺污水处理费价格机制，建立覆盖成本、保本微利的动态调整机制；引入第三方监测和成本监审，确保按效付费的公平性和可持续性。

5. **风险上**：建立外部不可控因素的风险分担机制，避免运营企业因非自身原因遭受过度惩罚，从而保护其参与改革的积极性。

最终目标是形成“精准投入—效益提升—成本节约—再投入”的良性循环。武汉、湘潭、沅江等地的实践证明，只要坚持系统治理、机制创新与数字赋能并重，市政污水收集处理完全可以在降低财政负担的同时，实现水环境质量的持续改善。

prompt: While the market features diverse quantitative strategies like multi-factor and high-frequency trading, it lacks a single, standardized benchmark for assessing their performance across multiple dimensions such as returns, risk, and adaptability to market conditions. Could we develop a general yet rigorous evaluation framework to enable accurate comparison and analysis of various advanced quant strategies?
article:
# Towards a Unified Quantitative Strategy Evaluation Framework (UQSEF): Moving Beyond the Singular Benchmark

**Abstract**

The quantitative investment landscape in 2026 is profoundly fragmented, spanning high-frequency trading (HFT), multi-factor models, systematic macro, event-driven strategies, and multi-manager platforms. Despite this sophistication, the industry lacks a standardized, multi-dimensional benchmark for comparing these disparate approaches. Traditional evaluation relies heavily on the Sharpe ratio or anecdotal backtest results, methodologies that are demonstrably inadequate for capturing the full risk, return, capacity, and adaptability profile of a strategy. This report synthesizes best practices from quantitative finance risk management, AI/ML evaluation science, and market structure analysis to propose a Unified Quantitative Strategy Evaluation Framework (UQSEF). The framework mandates Walk-Forward Optimization (WFO) as a foundational validation step, requires a multi-metric risk-adjusted return suite (Sortino, Calmar, Capacity), and incorporates an Adaptability Score to measure model decay. The UQSEF prioritizes traceability and reproducibility, moving the industry beyond the myth of a single benchmark towards a rigorous, contextualized evaluation protocol.

---

## 1. Introduction: The Fragmentation of Quantitative Finance

The quantitative finance industry in 2026 is characterized by a vast and growing bifurcation of strategies. The HFT market is projected to grow from $13.38 billion in 2025 to $21.46 billion by 2030, driven by advances in cloud computing, AI-driven algorithms, and ultra-low latency infrastructure ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/high-frequency-trading-business-report-094100804.html)). Simultaneously, the hedge fund industry is on a trajectory towards $5 trillion in assets under management, with multi-manager platforms facing capacity constraints that are creating opportunities for second-tier entrants ([WithIntelligence](https://www.withintelligence.com/insights/hedge-fund-outlook-2026)). Institutional investors remain cautiously optimistic, with 59% reporting they are modestly bullish about achieving target returns over the next decade, supported by diversified portfolios including alternative assets like REITs and private credit ([Commonfund](https://www.commonfund.org/research-center/press-releases/institutional-investors-lower-2026-return-expectations-amid-geopolitical-risks)).

Despite this remarkable sophistication, the industry operates without a universally accepted framework for comparing these fundamentally different strategies. A high-frequency market-making strategy generating a double-digit Sharpe ratio with a capacity of $500 million ([Kinlay](https://jonathankinlay.com/2018/12/high-frequency-trading-strategies)) is categorically different from a multi-factor strategy with a Sharpe of 1.5 and a capacity of $10 billion. The lack of a standardized benchmark creates significant risks for allocators, obscures meaningful comparison, and hinders scientific progress in the field.

---

## 2. The Limitations of Current Evaluation Practices

### 2.1. The Tyranny of the Sharpe Ratio

The Sharpe ratio, while ubiquitous, treats all volatility as risk. This penalizes strategies with high upside volatility, such as trend-following, and fails to capture the true risk profile of a portfolio. The Sortino ratio, which focuses solely on downside deviation, is often preferred for asymmetric return distributions ([XBTO](https://www.xbto.com/resources/sharpe-sortino-and-calmar-a-practical-guide-to-risk-adjusted-return-metrics-for-crypto-investors)). The Calmar ratio, using maximum drawdown as its risk measure, is particularly suitable for drawdown-averse institutional investors, though it can be misleading in bull markets without major drawdowns and is less statistically significant due to fewer data points ([Optimized Portfolio](https://www.optimizedportfolio.com/risk-adjusted-return)).

For institutional allocation, a strategy with strong Sortino and Calmar ratios (e.g., Fund B with Sortino 3.8, Calmar 2.0) is preferred over one with high raw returns but extreme drawdowns (Fund A with 80% drawdown), as it fits within risk budgets and allows investors to stay invested ([XBTO](https://www.xbto.com/resources/sharpe-sortino-and-calmar-a-practical-guide-to-risk-adjusted-return-metrics-for-crypto-investors)). A robust framework must mandate a suite of risk-adjusted metrics, not just a single one.

### 2.2. The Perils of Overfitting

Static backtesting provides a false sense of confidence. Walk-forward optimization (WFO) is a key technique to mitigate overfitting in ML-driven trading strategies, validating the strategy across rolling out-of-sample windows and reducing false confidence from a single validation period ([QuantInsti](https://blog.quantinsti.com/walk-forward-optimization-introduction)). Overfitting can be detected using a combination of WFO, parameter sensitivity heatmaps, and Monte Carlo trade sequencing ([LuxAlgo](https://www.luxalgo.com/blog/stress-test-your-algorithmic-trading-strategy-guide-to-avoiding-overfitting)).

A unified evaluation framework for quantitative strategies should include robust backtesting, performance attribution, and measures to mitigate overfitting and data snooping bias ([FinancialModelingPrep](https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/education/financial-ratios/Quantitative-Investment-Strategies-Backtesting-Performance-Attribution-and-Machine-Learning-Applications)). WFO is computationally intensive but irreplaceable; it must be mandated as the minimum standard for validation.

### 2.3. The Capacity and Decay Dimensions

Capacity is a critical, often overlooked dimension. HFT strategies have notoriously low capacity limits due to their reliance on fleeting market inefficiencies, with profitability critically dependent on high fill rates and low-latency infrastructure ([DayTrading](https://www.daytrading.com/trading-strategy-capacity); [Kinlay](https://jonathankinlay.com/2018/12/high-frequency-trading-strategies)). A strategy that performs excellently on a small account may fail entirely at scale due to market impact and increased competition.

Furthermore, financial models decay due to non-stationary markets. Production ML systems require monitoring dashboards that track prediction accuracy, feature importance stability, and realized versus predicted returns, with retraining schedules—weekly, monthly, or triggered by performance degradation—essential to maintain predictive power ([Quantt](https://www.quantt.co.uk/resources/machine-learning-finance-guide)). An evaluation framework must systematically measure a strategy's resistance to decay.

| Evaluation Dimension | Current Practice | Limitation | Proposed UQSEF Practice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation | Single backtest | Overfitting, false confidence | Mandatory Walk-Forward Optimization |
| Risk-Adjusted Returns | Sharpe ratio | Penalizes upside volatility | Sortino, Calmar, and Capacity metrics |
| Scalability | Ignored | Strategies fail at scale | Capacity Score |
| Model Resilience | Unmeasured | Blind to model decay | Adaptability Score |

---

## 3. Building Blocks for a Unified Framework

### 3.1. Standardized Validation Protocol: Mandating Walk-Forward Optimization

Any strategy submitted for evaluation under a unified framework must survive a rigorous WFO test. WFO reduces overfitting by testing each segment of data in a forward-looking manner, preventing the false confidence that can come from a single, potentially lucky validation period ([QuantInsti](https://blog.quantinsti.com/walk-forward-optimization-introduction)). The framework must define a standard for window size and step size, or at minimum require the strategy to be tested across multiple configurations to ensure robustness against window size selection bias.

### 3.2. Multi-Dimensional Performance Metrics

The framework should produce a standardized scorecard that captures the full spectrum of strategy performance. This approach borrows heavily from AI/ML evaluation science, where standardized evaluation frameworks provide unified interfaces, controlled experimental settings, and multi-dimensional evaluation encompassing efficiency, interpretability, and robustness to ensure reproducibility and comparability across tasks and domains ([EmergentMind](https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/standardized-evaluation-frameworks)).

The proposed scorecard includes:

1. **Walk-Forward Sortino Ratio**: Downside risk-adjusted return on out-of-sample data, focusing on harmful risk.
2. **Walk-Forward Calmar Ratio**: Risk-adjusted return using maximum drawdown, critical for drawdown-averse allocators.
3. **Capacity Score**: Estimated AUM at which performance degrades by a defined threshold, addressing scalability.
4. **Adaptability Score**: Rolling window stability of the core performance metric, measuring resistance to model decay.

### 3.3. Integration of AI/ML Evaluation Best Practices

The evaluation framework must prioritize traceability, linking evaluation scores to specific versions of prompts, models, and datasets ([FutureAGI](https://futureagi.substack.com/p/llm-evaluation-frameworks-metrics)). Best practices for AI evaluation include defining success metrics early, tracking multiple metrics, evaluating on both validation and production data, and monitoring metrics over time to catch regressions and adapt to data drift ([Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/glossary/ml-evaluation-metrics)). This translates directly to quant finance: track the specific feature set, market regime, and transaction cost model used in the WFO.

### 3.4. Regime Awareness and Contextualization

A general framework must contextualize performance against market regimes. Alternative data, such as NLP-derived sentiment and emotion indicators from news and social media, can provide a premium in quantitative strategies, enabling both Long Only and Long/Short portfolio construction ([Informa Connect](https://informaconnect.com/alternative-data-in-quantitative-strategies-use-cases)). Machine learning models (e.g., SVM, random forest) can outperform traditional approaches in predictive accuracy, but their real-world effectiveness is constrained by transaction costs, model decay, and interpretability challenges ([IJFMR](https://www.ijfmr.com/research-paper.php?id=65636)). The framework must label the market regime during which the evaluation was conducted to prevent misleading comparisons across different market environments.

---

## 4. A Concrete Proposal: The UQSEF Prototype

The Unified Quantitative Strategy Evaluation Framework (UQSEF) is proposed as a three-layer protocol:

### Layer 1: Validation (WFO)
The strategy must survive a purged walk-forward analysis. This is the gatekeeping function. No strategy can proceed to Layer 2 without demonstrating robust out-of-sample performance.

### Layer 2: Multi-Dimensional Scoring
The strategy is scored on a standard report card encompassing Sortino, Calmar, Capacity, and Adaptability. No single score is used to rank strategies; instead, a profile is generated that highlights trade-offs.

### Layer 3: Contextualization and Traceability
The evaluation must be performed against a standard set of market regimes (e.g., high volatility, low volatility, trending, mean-reverting). The exact data specifications, feature sets, and model versions must be logged to ensure reproducibility.

### Example: Comparing HFT vs. Multi-Factor under UQSEF

| Metric | HFT Strategy | Multi-Factor Strategy |
|---|---|---|
| WFO Sortino Ratio | 4.5 | 1.8 |
| Capacity Score | \$500M | \$10B |
| Adaptability Score | High (constantly recalibrates) | Moderate (slow factor decay) |
| Regime Context | High-vol, fragmented markets | Trending, low-vol markets |

Under UQSEF, a direct comparison is irrelevant. The framework highlights the trade-offs involved. An allocator with a \$200M risk budget seeking high returns might prefer the HFT strategy. An allocator with a \$5B pension fund seeking stable, scalable beta would prefer the Multi-Factor strategy. The framework enables informed decision-making rather than misleading ranking.

---

## 5. Challenges and Implementation Hurdles

Implementing UQSEF faces significant hurdles. The computational complexity of WFO is high, especially for complex or high-frequency strategies ([QuantInsti](https://blog.quantinsti.com/walk-forward-optimization-introduction)). Standardizing "market regimes" is inherently difficult and subjective, requiring careful calibration.

Many firms are resistant to sharing the detailed data required for rigorous traceability, citing proprietary concerns. However, the allocator community is increasingly demanding such transparency. The recent trend of managers providing separately managed accounts (SMAs) and greater transparency, with tier-two multi-manager platforms gaining ground as larger peers face capacity constraints, suggests the industry is moving in this direction ([WithIntelligence](https://www.withintelligence.com/insights/hedge-fund-outlook-2026)).

The HFT market faces additional challenges from regulatory scrutiny and broker restrictions on scalping and hyperactivity strategies, with proprietary trading firms increasingly specifying what automated short-term activity they will tolerate ([Young & Calculated](https://youngandcalculated.substack.com/p/high-frequency-trading-explained)). The framework must account for these operational constraints.

---

## 6. Conclusion: The Path Forward

The pursuit of a single, monolithic benchmark for quantitative strategies is a misguided objective that leads to false comparisons and misallocated capital. The correct path forward is the adoption of a rigorous, multi-dimensional evaluation protocol.

The proposed Unified Quantitative Strategy Evaluation Framework (UQSEF) synthesizes the best of quantitative finance risk management and AI/ML evaluation science. By mandating Walk-Forward Optimization, employing a multi-dimensional risk-return scorecard, and prioritizing traceability and reproducibility, UQSEF provides the rigorous, comparative analysis the industry desperately needs.

This report concludes that a single numeric benchmark for quantitative strategies is a myth. The diversity of strategies—from HFT exploiting microsecond inefficiencies to multi-manager platforms allocating across hundreds of sub-strategies—makes a single metric impossible. However, a rigorous, standardized evaluation protocol is not only feasible but essential for the continued maturation of the industry.

Allocators should demand this protocol; researchers should build upon it. The path forward is not a single number, but a standardized, transparent, and multi-dimensional approach to evaluation that reflects the true complexity of modern quantitative finance.

article:
# Enhancing PID Control Performance for UAV Attitude Control: Adaptive Methods and Optimal Parameter Selection

## Abstract

Quadrotor UAVs present a challenging control problem due to their nonlinear, strongly coupled, and underactuated dynamics ([Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html)). While cascaded PID controllers dominate open-source flight controllers, fixed-gain PID performance degrades across diverse flight conditions. This report synthesizes recent research on adaptive PID variants—fuzzy logic, neural networks, hybrid architectures, and metaheuristic optimization—and proposes a practical pathway for improving real-world PID control performance.

## 1. Introduction

Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), particularly quadrotors, are increasingly deployed in surveillance, logistics, disaster response, and smart infrastructure applications ([ICAIIT, 2026](http://icaiit.org/proceedings/14th_ICAIIT_1/8-1-ICAIIT_2026_14(1).pdf)). The attitude control problem is central to stable flight: quadrotor dynamics are nonlinear, strongly coupled, and underactuated, making precise attitude control crucial for mission success ([Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html)). Most open-source flight controllers implement a cascade PID architecture—an outer attitude loop feeding an inner angular velocity loop—because of its simplicity and established effectiveness ([Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html); [Yue, 2026](https://drpress.org/ojs/index.php/ajst/article/view/33317)). However, a single fixed set of PID gains typically performs well only under specific flight conditions. This report examines methods to enhance PID control performance and how PID parameters should be optimally selected.

## 2. The Cascade PID Architecture in UAV Attitude Control

Cascade PID control is a widely used strategy for managing systems affected by both fast and slow disturbances. For quadrotors, the architecture employs an outer loop for attitude control (producing desired angular rates) and an inner loop for angular velocity control ([Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html)). This nested structure allows the inner loop to correct fast disturbances before they propagate to the outer loop, improving overall stability ([ControlSoft, n.d.](https://www.controlsoftinc.com/tuning-cascade-loops-2)).

A key tuning principle emerges from process control practice: the inner (secondary) loop must be tuned before the outer (primary) loop, and a simple proportional-integral (PI) controller is often sufficient for the inner loop ([ControlSoft, n.d.](https://www.controlsoftinc.com/tuning-cascade-loops-2)). For quadrotors, this translates to tuning the angular velocity loop first—typically with fast dynamics—and then the attitude loop.

## 3. Limitations of Fixed-Gain PID

Despite its dominance—PID controllers account for 90–97% of UAV control applications ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html))—classical PID has well-documented weaknesses:

- **Fixed gains cannot adapt** to nonlinear dynamics, varying system parameters, and unpredictable external disturbances ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).
- **Disturbance sensitivity**: An Arduino-based UAV prototype required approximately 20 seconds to stabilize after disturbance, with stability dropping from 97% under minor disturbances to 70–80% under stronger winds ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)).
- **Manual tuning is suboptimal**: Traditional PID parameter tuning relies heavily on manual experience and often yields suboptimal performance ([Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html)).

Lopez-Sanchez and Moreno-Valenzuela concluded that PID with fixed parameters ensures stable operation only in disturbance-free environments, while nonlinear or time-varying dynamics require hybrid, adaptive, or intelligent extensions for long-term reliability ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)).

## 4. Methods for Enhancing PID Control Performance

### 4.1 Fuzzy Logic-Based Adaptive PID (FPID)

Fuzzy PID controllers integrate a fuzzy inference system with traditional PID to adjust gains (Kp, Ki, Kd) in real time based on error and error derivative. Rather than relying on exact mathematical models, fuzzy logic uses rule-based inference, making it effective in handling uncertain, variable environments ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)).

Quantitative evidence strongly supports FPID efficacy:

| Metric | Classical PID | Fuzzy PID | Improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rise time (noise-free) | 3.29 s | 2.03 s | 38% faster |
| Overshoot (noise-free) | 55.74% | 50.30% | 9.8% lower |
| Steady-state error (noise-free) | 0.0365 m | 0.0315 m | 13.7% lower |
| Steady-state error (with noise) | 1.0272 m | 0.4060 m | **60.5% reduction** |
| MSE under wind disturbance (z-axis) | — | — | **87.49% reduction** |

([Vo Van An, 2026](https://www.aimspress.com/article/id/6a2a4647ba35de0d193b2bb7))

In agricultural UAV applications, fuzzy PID improved altitude, velocity, and lateral tilt control by 11–44% on average compared with classical PID ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)). A cascaded fuzzy-PID architecture for low-cost quadrotors reduced pitch/roll stabilization time by 45%, yaw stabilization time by 31%, and recovery time to stability by 44% under identical disturbance conditions, while remaining computationally efficient enough for ARM Cortex-M3 embedded deployment ([Yue, 2026](https://drpress.org/ojs/index.php/ajst/article/view/33317)).

However, standalone FPID has limitations: it offers heuristic adaptability but lacks precision for certain dynamic states ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)). A common FPID implementation uses five fuzzy sets (negative big, negative small, zero, positive small, positive big) with 125 rules, Mamdani inference, and centroid defuzzification ([AZoRobotics, n.d.](https://www.azorobotics.com/News.aspx?newsID=14819)).

### 4.2 Neural Network-Based PID (NNPID)

Neural network PID controllers use a neural network to fine-tune PID parameters online. A single-layer network with 10 hidden neurons and nonlinear sigmoid activation, trained via gradient descent minimizing mean squared error, can adjust PID gains for high-precision states ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).

NNPID demonstrates extremely low MSE values for states requiring high trajectory accuracy (e.g., y and ψ), maintaining near-perfect performance even under disturbances. However, it is computationally intensive and less flexible in real-time scenarios compared to fuzzy approaches ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).

A hybrid ANN-PID controller, where the neural network dynamically adjusts PID coefficients, achieved the lowest steady-state error (0.0229 m) compared to classical PID and LQR controllers in simulation ([Vo Van An et al., 2026](https://www.aimspress.com/article/doi/10.3934/electreng.2026002?viewType=HTML)).

### 4.3 Hybrid Neural-Fuzzy PID (NNPID+FPID)

The most compelling advancement is the hybrid NNPID+FPID strategy. This approach leverages the strengths of both methods:

- **Neural networks** tune PID gains for y and ψ states, where precision is critical.
- **Fuzzy logic** tunes gains for x, z, φ, and θ states, providing real-time adaptability and stability.

The hybrid approach demonstrates superior trajectory tracking and system stability across all six UAV dynamic states compared to standalone NNPID and FPID methods ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)). This addresses a critical research gap: standalone methods struggle with full-state nonlinear tracking, and the hybrid architecture provides the optimal balance of stability, adaptability, and performance ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).

Similarly, hybrid Fuzzy-PID controllers significantly outperform both classical PID and fuzzy-only controllers in terms of RMSE, overshoot, and settling time, with faster error convergence and smoother control inputs while maintaining robustness against wind gusts and sensor noise ([ICAIIT, 2026](http://icaiit.org/proceedings/14th_ICAIIT_1/8-1-ICAIIT_2026_14(1).pdf)). For fixed-wing UAVs, combined ANFIS-PID and PD-fuzzy-PI controllers demonstrated more acceptable performance than classical PID at steady-level flight ([Ulus & Eski, 2021](https://avesis.erciyes.edu.tr/yayin/eff3c364-0eed-4e81-83f5-16e1a638367b/neural-network-and-fuzzy-logic-based-hybrid-attitude-controller-designs-of-a-fixed-wing-uav)).

### 4.4 Other Advanced PID Variants

Fractional-order PID (FOPID) and machine-learning-optimized controllers offer significant improvements in robustness, stability, and response time compared to classical PID ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)). Advanced methods such as sliding mode control and model predictive control provide more effective performance in nonlinear systems and in the presence of disturbances, though they increase computational complexity.

## 5. Optimal PID Parameter Selection

### 5.1 Metaheuristic Optimization

Traditional PID tuning methods (e.g., Ziegler-Nichols) provide only acceptable performance and require fine-tuning. Metaheuristic algorithms have emerged as a robust alternative for optimizing cascade PID gains.

An improved particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm integrating:

- **Adaptive inertia weight**
- **Dynamic learning factors**
- **Latin hypercube sampling**

has been shown to effectively tune cascade PID controllers for quadrotor attitude control, improving settling time and reducing overshoot ([Cheng, 2025](https://doi.org/10.71222/4eamzx24); [Cheng, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/dba/ejacia/v1y2025i3p102-111.html)).

Metaheuristic-based tuning of cascade PID gains can identify optimal gains that minimize objective functions and provide robust trajectory tracking under bounded disturbances and parametric uncertainties ([Çopur et al., 2025](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/aeronautical-journal/article/tuning-of-cascade-pid-controller-gains-of-quadcopter-under-bounded-disturbances-using-metaheuristic-based-research-algorithm/A8CE601210ACADB2F8D99C827188D480)). For fixed-wing UAVs, artificial bee colony (ABC) optimization of cascade PID gains found that the IAE fitness function yielded the optimum result for altitude control among ITAE, ISE, MSE, and IAE criteria ([Durmaz et al., 2023](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/ems/article/1243796)).

The PSO algorithm works by iteratively updating particle positions and velocities based on personal and collective best performances, with the velocity update equation:

$$v_{t+1} = \omega v_t + 2R_1(p_i - x_t) + 2R_2(g - x_t)$$

where ω is the inertia weight, R₁ is the cognitive weight, and R₂ is the social weight ([Semantic Scholar, 2025](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/dae5/55def4ddd7aac965ecf060837de4cf8b4b05.pdf)).

### 5.2 Cascade Loop Tuning Principles

For cascade control structures, several practical rules apply:

1. **Tune the inner loop first**: PID 2 (inner) before PID 1 (outer), with the inner loop in control when tuning the outer loop.
2. **PI is often sufficient for the inner loop**: A simple proportional-integral controller handles the fast inner dynamics effectively ([ControlSoft, n.d.](https://www.controlsoftinc.com/tuning-cascade-loops-2)).
3. **Prevent windup**: When the inner loop saturates, the outer controller must be inhibited to avoid integral windup ([ControlSoft, n.d.](https://www.controlsoftinc.com/tuning-cascade-loops-2)).
4. **Optimize both loops simultaneously**: Metaheuristic tuning can optimize both outer and inner loop gains together rather than sequentially ([Cheng, 2025](https://doi.org/10.71222/4eamzx24)).

### 5.3 Practical Parameter Selection Recommendations

Based on the synthesized evidence, a concrete parameter selection strategy should:

1. **Use metaheuristic optimization (improved PSO or ABC) offline** to find initial cascade PID gains, minimizing objective functions like IAE or ITAE rather than relying on manual experience.
2. **Select the objective function carefully**: IAE proved optimal for altitude control in fixed-wing UAV studies ([Durmaz et al., 2023](https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/ems/article/1243796)); MSE-based criteria are useful for disturbance rejection tuning.
3. **Layer adaptive mechanisms on optimized gains**: Rather than choosing between fixed-gain PID and adaptive PID, use optimized gains as the baseline and add fuzzy logic or neural network tuning on top for real-time adaptation. This hybrid approach proved superior to either method alone ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).
4. **Match the adaptive method to state dynamics**: Use neural networks for states requiring high precision (y, ψ) and fuzzy logic for states needing robust real-time adaptation (x, z, φ, θ) ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).

## 6. Validation: From Simulation to Hardware-in-the-Loop

A critical limitation in the literature is the predominance of simulation-based studies. Many hybrid Fuzzy-PID and metaheuristic-tuning studies lack real-time experimental validation ([ICAIIT, 2026](http://icaiit.org/proceedings/14th_ICAIIT_1/8-1-ICAIIT_2026_14(1).pdf); [Çopur et al., 2025](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/aeronautical-journal/article/tuning-of-cascade-pid-controller-gains-of-quadcopter-under-bounded-disturbances-using-metaheuristic-based-research-algorithm/A8CE601210ACADB2F8D99C827188D480)).

Controller Hardware-in-the-Loop (C-HIL) simulation provides a practical intermediate validation step. A C-HIL framework executing a quadcopter attitude plant model in an OPAL-RT real-time environment with a discrete PID controller (PI for yaw) on a TI LaunchXL-F280049C microcontroller at 1 kHz achieved stable tracking with small steady-state error while exposing real-time implementation effects such as quantization, saturation, and closed-loop latency ([Abdelrazeq & Ahmad, 2026](https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/hardware-in-the-loop-simulation-of-a-3-dof-quadcopter)). Key implementation details—models, scaling, I/O mapping, and end-to-end timing—must be documented for reproducible and meaningful HIL validation ([Abdelrazeq & Ahmad, 2026](https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/hardware-in-the-loop-simulation-of-a-3-dof-quadcopter)).

For low-cost platforms, computational efficiency is a binding constraint. The cascaded fuzzy-PID architecture demonstrated computational efficiency satisfying embedded deployment requirements on ARM Cortex-M3 platforms ([Yue, 2026](https://drpress.org/ojs/index.php/ajst/article/view/33317)), suggesting that fuzzy-based adaptation is practical even on resource-constrained hardware.

## 7. Conclusions and Recommendations

Based on the synthesized evidence, the following concrete conclusions emerge:

**First**, classical fixed-gain PID is insufficient for UAV attitude control across diverse flight conditions. The evidence is unambiguous: PID controllers exhibit overshoot, longer settling times, and inability to maintain stability under strong disturbances ([Opast Publishers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/pid-control-and-alternative-control-approaches-in-uav-systems-9726.html)).

**Second**, the most effective enhancement strategy is a hybrid approach that combines offline metaheuristic optimization with online adaptive gain tuning. Metaheuristic algorithms (particularly improved PSO with adaptive inertia weight, dynamic learning factors, and Latin hypercube sampling) provide near-optimal baseline gains ([Cheng, 2025](https://doi.org/10.71222/4eamzx24)), while fuzzy logic or neural networks adjust gains in real time to handle disturbances and parameter variations. The hybrid NNPID+FPID strategy, which assigns neural networks to precision-critical states and fuzzy logic to robustness-critical states, represents the current state of the art ([Madebo, 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0331036)).

**Third**, parameter selection must be treated as a two-stage process: offline optimization (using IAE or ITAE objective functions) followed by online adaptation. Practitioners should adopt cascade tuning principles—inner loop first, PI for the inner loop, anti-windup protection—and combine them with simultaneous multi-loop metaheuristic optimization ([ControlSoft, n.d.](https://www.controlsoftinc.com/tuning-cascade-loops-2); [Cheng, 2025](https://doi.org/10.71222/4eamzx24)).

**Fourth**, validation should progress through simulation and C-HIL before deployment. C-HIL at 1 kHz with real microcontrollers exposes quantization, saturation, and latency effects that pure simulations miss ([Abdelrazeq & Ahmad, 2026](https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/hardware-in-the-loop-simulation-of-a-3-dof-quadcopter)).

The path forward for open-source flight controllers is not to abandon PID but to make it adaptive and optimized. Given the 87.49% MSE reduction under wind disturbances ([Vo Van An, 2026](https://www.aimspress.com/article/id/6a2a4647ba35de0d193b2bb7)) and the 60.5% steady-state error reduction under noise, hybrid fuzzy-PID with metaheuristic-optimized baseline gains offers the most practical, computationally feasible route to robust UAV attitude control across diverse flight states.

## References

# 国内金融机构投资借贷关系与系统性风险：多层次建模研究综述

## 摘要

本文系统梳理了中国金融机构之间投资借贷关系的类型、规模及其与系统性风险的联系，重点评述不同层次（宏观市场、微观机构、跨尺度）和不同类型（同业拆借、回购、同业存单、交叉持股、共同资产持有）借贷关系的风险建模方法。研究发现：多层网络模型能够捕捉单层网络遗漏的风险叠加效应；动态宏观压力测试必须纳入资产抛售和价格反馈；短期与长期借贷的区分对风险估计有显著影响。据此，本文提出建立“三层三通道”动态监测框架，并对不同借贷类型实施差异化监管工具。

## 1. 引言

金融机构之间的投资借贷关系是系统性风险传染的核心渠道。在中国，银行间市场是短期资金融通的主要场所，其规模与结构直接影响金融体系稳定性。传统的单机构、单渠道监管已难以应对日益复杂的交叉关联，因此需要从多层次、多类型的借贷关系出发，构建能够刻画非线性传染和动态演化的风险模型。

## 2. 国内金融机构间借贷关系的类型与规模

### 2.1 银行间同业拆借与回购市场

中国银行间回购市场是短期融资的重要来源，未偿余额约5万亿元人民币（约7200亿美元），约为美国回购市场的三分之一（[RBA, 2017](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2017/jun/pdf/bu-0617-9-the-chinese-interbank-repo-market.pdf)）。与欧美主要市场不同，中国银行间回购以质押式为主，而非买断式。质押式回购中抵押品不能出售，投资者无法通过借入等价债券来平仓，这限制了风险对冲能力，也改变了风险动态（[RBA, 2017](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2017/jun/pdf/bu-0617-9-the-chinese-interbank-repo-market.pdf)）。抵押品高度集中于政府债券和政策性银行债券，占比近90%；政策银行在回购贷款余额中的份额从2014年初的约20%升至2015年初的近40%（[RBA, 2017](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2017/jun/pdf/bu-0617-9-the-chinese-interbank-repo-market.pdf)）。

同业拆借网络呈现核心-边缘结构，系统重要性银行位于核心。若仅使用短期借贷数据而忽略长期借贷，会低估市场条件恶化时的系统性风险（[Jin et al., 2024](https://ideas.repec.org/a/spr/empeco/v67y2024i6d10.1007_s00181-024-02617-9.html)）。

### 2.2 同业存单与批发融资

近年来，同业存单成为非国有银行重要的批发融资工具。研究表明，同业存单虽然改善了货币政策向非国有银行的传导，但也导致其财务脆弱性快速上升；自2018年以来，对同业存单依赖较高的非国有银行在负面经济冲击下表现出更大的系统性风险（[PHBS, 2024](https://english.phbs.pku.edu.cn/info/3281/16731.htm)）。这体现了批发融资在提升效率与增加脆弱性之间的权衡。

### 2.3 交叉持股与共同资产持有

除直接借贷外，金融机构之间还通过交叉持股和共同资产持有形成隐性关联。基于中国162家金融机构数据的双层网络分析表明，仅考虑银行间借贷会低估系统性风险，因为交叉持股渠道会与借贷渠道产生非线性叠加效应（[Zou et al., 2019](https://www.jasss.org/22/4/9.html)）。类似地，包含银行间借贷、交叉持股和共同资产持有的三层网络模型发现，多层结构对系统性损失具有非线性叠加效应，其中银行间借贷和共同资产持有是主要风险传染源（[Yan et al., 2023](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/phsmap/v628y2023ics0378437123006994.html)）。

## 3. 系统性风险传染机制

### 3.1 直接传染渠道

直接传染源于机构间的资产负债联系。当一家机构违约时，其债权人的资产质量直接受损。银行间市场是这种传染最突出的渠道，它连接了银行的资产负债表，并迅速将一个机构的困境传播至整个系统（[Bowe et al., n.d.](https://www.bis.org/ifc/events/ws_micro_macro/bowe_paper.pdf)）。此外，支付系统渠道和资产收益率渠道也是重要的直接传染路径（[刘亚轩, 2026](https://www.fcipub.org/articleDetail/4045?periodicalId=30)）。

### 3.2 间接传染：价格渠道与火售

火售（fire sales）和去杠杆反馈是宏观压力测试必须纳入的关键机制。火售溢出通过价格中介，因此无法通过交易对手限额或机构隔离措施来遏制（[Cont & Schaanning, n.d.](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/086b/44fc818fda2c9a4c06255039560fd7d4079e.pdf)）。在资本充足率约束下，银行的最优抛售行为可能加剧系统范围内的风险传染；金融风险的演化呈非线性，判断风险阶段对监管至关重要（[马骏 & 何晓贝, 2021](http://www.jryj.org.cn/CN/abstract/abstract937.shtml)）。

### 3.3 信息与信心传染

即使基本面没有变化，信念改变也可能导致多重均衡和挤兑。金融网络的复杂性使投资者难以评估对手方风险，从而可能高估风险并撤回资金，形成自我实现的预言（[金融网络中的系统性风险综述, 2022](https://bijiao.caixin.com/m/2022-05-06/101881413_all.html)）。

### 3.4 多层叠加与非线性

双层网络研究表明，传染损失大于银行间借贷网络和交叉持股网络独立传染损失之和，且超额损失主要由银行间借贷渠道造成；若交叉持股渠道增强，超额损失趋于增加（[Zou et al., 2019](https://www.jasss.org/22/4/9.html)）。这表明风险在不同渠道间不是简单相加，而是非线性放大。

## 4. 不同层次借贷关系的风险建模方法

### 4.1 单层网络模型

早期研究常用最小生成树（MST）和平面极大过滤图（PMFG）构建银行间同业拆借网络，动态识别系统重要性节点，并利用MST的唯一性直观展示风险传导路径（[欧阳红兵 & 刘晓东, 2015](https://www.zgglkx.com/CN/Y2015/V23/I10/30)）。这类方法计算简便，但只能刻画单一关系，可能遗漏其他渠道的风险。

### 4.2 多层网络模型

多层网络模型将银行间借贷、交叉持股、共同资产持有等不同关系作为独立层，能够识别单层网络遗漏的系统重要性机构，并揭示不同层对系统性风险的差异化贡献（[FCPI, n.d.](https://www.fcpi.org/articleDetail/2645?periodicalId=55)）。例如，将DebtRank模型扩展至三层网络后，发现中国四大国有商业银行是系统重要性银行，且制造业、交通运输业和个人信贷的贷款余额应成为监测重点（[Yan et al., 2023](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/phsmap/v628y2023ics0378437123006994.html)）。银行-企业多层网络还揭示了金融与实体部门之间的风险反馈效应（[Lei et al., 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/phsmap/v675y2025ics037843712500490x.html)）。

### 4.3 动态网络模型

多尺度动态网络模型将DCC-GARCH动态相关系数作为宏观跨市场边权，将CoVaR风险溢出值作为微观跨主体边权，将回归系数作为跨尺度边权，从而构建覆盖多维度、多主体的风险传导网络（[wispace, n.d.](https://wispace.cc/thesis/economic_theses/chinese_economy_theses/systemic-financial-risk-transmission-china-multi-scale-model)）。研究发现，在市场剧烈波动或外部冲击明显阶段，网络密度急剧上升、核心节点地位显著强化，风险传导速度与广度随之放大（[wispace, n.d.](https://wispace.cc/thesis/economic_theses/chinese_economy_theses/systemic-financial-risk-transmission-china-multi-scale-model)）。动态网络模拟还显示，内部冲击首先在同行业内传播，再扩散至其他行业；外部冲击则先传导至银行，再至多元化金融机构、证券和保险机构（[Xie & Li, n.d.](https://scienceon.kisti.re.kr/srch/selectPORSrchArticle.do?cn=NART124857229)）。

### 4.4 宏观压力测试与火售建模

静态银行压力测试只能看到冲击发生期的直接效应，无法预判随后几期的传染效应，会大大低估风险评估（[马骏 & 何晓贝, 2021](http://www.jryj.org.cn/CN/abstract/abstract937.shtml)）。因此，需要构建动态的、模拟金融风险传染的宏观审慎压力测试（[马骏 & 何晓贝, 2021](http://www.jryj.org.cn/CN/abstract/abstract937.shtml)）。火售模型通过组合持有、杠杆约束和市场冲击反应函数来量化价格中介的传染，并发现火售损失可占压力情景总损失的35%以上，足以改变压力测试结果（[Cont & Schaanning, n.d.](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/086b/44fc818fda2c9a4c06255039560fd7d4079e.pdf)）。对宏观审慎压力测试的回测也表明，适当校准的模型比不考虑共同资产持有网络的基准模型具有更强的预测能力（[Bundesbank, 2020](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/840860/e805a086ad5b53907ef2f357bcea239b/mL/2020-08-12-dkp-45-data.pdf)）。此外，压力测试还可加入融资溢出等宏观审慎元素，以捕捉金融部门内部及金融与实体之间的反馈（[Bassett & Rappoport, 2022](https://www.bostonfed.org/-/media/Documents/events/2022/FR-STRC/Enhancing-Stress-Tests-by-Adding-Macroprudential-Elements.pdf)）。

### 4.5 系统重要性度量与政策权衡

SRISK通过规模、杠杆、关联性和传染渠道捕捉系统性风险，被监管机构用于识别系统重要性金融机构和设计逆周期资本缓冲（[NYU V-Lab, n.d.](https://vlab.stern.nyu.edu/zh/docs/srisk)）。CoVaR方法则可同时度量系统性重要性（ΔCoVaR）和系统性脆弱性（Exposure-ΔCoVaR），提供更全面的评估（[李政等, 2019](https://html.rhhz.net/CJYJ/html/e9a58faf-810b-4115-993c-8cde81a2256d.htm)）。在政策层面，存在降低央行救助预期与提高银行资本要求之间的替代效应，这构成系统性风险监管的政策权衡（[Bowe et al., n.d.](https://www.bis.org/ifc/events/ws_micro_macro/bowe_paper.pdf)）。

下表总结了不同借贷/关联类型对应的风险渠道、建模方法与关键发现：

| 借贷/关联类型 | 主要风险渠道 | 建模方法 | 关键发现 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 银行间同业拆借 | 直接违约传染 | 单层/多层网络、DebtRank | 核心-边缘结构，忽略长期借贷低估风险 |
| 质押式回购 | 流动性风险、抵押品集中 | 市场微观结构分析 | 抵押品不可再使用限制对冲 |
| 同业存单 | 批发融资脆弱性 | 面板回归、系统性风险度量 | 增加非国有银行风险 |
| 交叉持股 | 间接传染、非线性叠加 | 双层网络 | 低估风险 |
| 共同资产持有 | 价格传染、火售 | 压力测试、火售模型 | 损失占比高，无法用对手方限额遏制 |

## 5. 实证发现与政策启示

### 5.1 中国系统重要性机构与行业敞口

多层网络分析一致表明，中国四大国有商业银行处于系统重要性核心位置，其贷款在制造业、交通运输业和个人信贷领域的集中度值得重点关注（[Yan et al., 2023](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/phsmap/v628y2023ics0378437123006994.html)）。网络中心性分析也发现，城市商业银行和金融租赁公司在特定时期可能表现出较强的系统重要性，这与业务扩张和市场地位变化有关（[FCPI, 2026](https://www.fcipub.org/articleDetail/2625?periodicalId=15)）。

### 5.2 网络密度与传染的非线性

网络密度具有“双刃剑”效应：密度较小时有利于风险分散，密度较大时则加快风险传播（[FCPI, 2026](https://www.fcipub.org/articleDetail/2625?periodicalId=15)）。金融网络中的传染在密度上具有非单调性，增加交易对手既可能增加风险来源，也可能通过分散敞口降低单一对手风险（[金融网络中的系统性风险综述, 2022](https://bijiao.caixin.com/m/2022-05-06/101881413_all.html)）。因此，监管不能简单追求“去连接”，而应关注网络结构的动态变化。

### 5.3 监管框架建议

基于上述研究，监管机构应构建覆盖再保险、共同资产等多维度的风险监测体系，对系统重要性机构实施差异化宏观审慎监管，并建立名单的动态调整机制（[FCPI, n.d.](https://www.fcpi.org/articleDetail/2645?periodicalId=55)）。中国《金融法（草案）》也体现了“所有金融活动”纳入监管、穿透式监管股东和实际控制人的趋势（[WilmerHale, 2026](https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/client-alerts/20260415-chinas-draft-financial-law-and-key-regulatory-insights)）。

## 6. 结论与观点

现有研究已经表明，中国金融机构之间的投资借贷关系通过直接违约、价格传染和信息反馈等渠道与系统性风险紧密相连，且不同层次、不同类型的借贷关系具有异质性的风险贡献。然而，多数监管实践仍以单层、静态压力测试为主，可能低估风险。

基于此，本文提出以下具体观点：

1. **建立“三层三通道”动态监测框架**。三层指宏观市场层（股市、债市、汇市、同业市场）、微观机构层（银行、证券、保险、基金）和跨尺度联动层；三通道指直接借贷违约、共同资产价格传染、交叉持股与信息反馈。该框架应利用DCC-GARCH、CoVaR和回归系数等边权设定，实现跨市场、跨机构、跨尺度的风险传导追踪（[wispace, n.d.](https://wispace.cc/thesis/economic_theses/chinese_economy_theses/systemic-financial-risk-transmission-china-multi-scale-model)）。

2. **针对不同借贷类型设置差异化工具**。对同业存单等短期批发融资设置流动性覆盖率附加和期限错配指标；对质押式回购应监测抵押品集中度和政策银行份额变化，并考虑抵押品不可再使用对市场流动性的抑制效应（[RBA, 2017](https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2017/jun/pdf/bu-0617-9-the-chinese-interbank-repo-market.pdf)）；对长期借贷则需纳入多期传染模拟（[Jin et al., 2024](https://ideas.repec.org/a/spr/empeco/v67y2024i6d10.1007_s00181-024-02617-9.html)）。

3. **宏观审慎压力测试必须内生化资产抛售和价格反馈**，而非仅依赖外生冲击放大；同时应定期回测模型预测能力，以选择最有效的风险度量工具（[Cont & Schaanning, n.d.](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/086b/44fc818fda2c9a4c06255039560fd7d4079e.pdf)；[Bundesbank, 2020](https://www.bundesbank.de/resource/blob/840860/e805a086ad5b53907ef2f357bcea239b/mL/2020-08-12-dkp-45-data.pdf)）。

4. **监管政策需权衡央行救助预期与资本要求**。过度依赖救助会滋生道德风险，但单纯提高资本要求可能抑制流动性创造，应通过动态校准实现平衡（[Bowe et al., n.d.](https://www.bis.org/ifc/events/ws_micro_macro/bowe_paper.pdf)）。

总之，只有将多层网络、动态演化和价格内生反馈纳入统一框架，才能更准确地评估中国金融体系的系统性风险，并为差异化监管提供科学依据。

# 中性粒细胞在脑缺血急性期与慢性期的功能动态、亚群互作及临床转化前景：基于近年研究的整合分析

## 摘要

缺血性脑卒中（ischemic stroke, IS）是全球范围内导致死亡和长期残疾的主要原因之一。近年研究揭示，中性粒细胞并非单纯的“第一反应者”，而是一个在时间、空间和功能上高度异质的细胞群体。本文整合了从分子机制、单细胞转录组、细胞间互作到临床结局预测的多层次证据，系统梳理了中性粒细胞在脑缺血急性期与慢性期的功能演变，重点分析了N1/N2极化、NETs形成、PKM2/STAT3通路、CD39及CXCR4信号等关键调控节点，并进一步预测中性粒细胞亚群与巨噬细胞、小胶质细胞、T细胞及血管内皮细胞的相互作用如何导向不同的临床结局。最后，本文提出未来研究应聚焦于亚群靶向、时序特异性干预、可靠生物标志物开发以及血管危险因素综合管理。

---

## 1. 引言

缺血性脑卒中约占所有卒中的80%–85%，其病理过程涉及兴奋性毒性、氧化应激、神经炎症和血脑屏障破坏等多种机制（[Levinson et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/surgery/articles/10.3389/fsurg.2025.1501359/full)）。中性粒细胞是外周血中最丰富的白细胞，也是缺血后最早进入脑实质的血源性免疫细胞，在损伤后数分钟至数小时内即可被募集到缺血区域（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。然而，中性粒细胞在脑缺血中的作用具有显著的双向性：一方面，它们通过释放活性氧（ROS）、蛋白酶、基质金属蛋白酶（MMPs）和中性粒细胞胞外陷阱（NETs）加剧组织损伤；另一方面，特定亚群如N2型中性粒细胞又参与组织修复和血管新生（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。因此，理解中性粒细胞在急性期和慢性期的功能演变及其与其他细胞的互作，对于开发新的治疗策略至关重要。

---

## 2. 中性粒细胞在脑缺血急性期与慢性期的时空动态

### 2.1 急性期：早期浸润与损伤放大

中性粒细胞在IS后的时间动态已被较为清晰地刻画。循环中性粒细胞计数在缺血后4–6小时即开始升高，6–8小时后开始向脑实质迁移；NETs在2–3天后可被检测到，中性粒细胞浸润在1–3天达到高峰，并在7–15天后仍可检测到表达，之后逐渐下降（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。这种持续存在提示中性粒细胞不仅参与急性损伤，也可能在亚急性期和慢性期发挥调节作用。

急性期中性粒细胞通过多种机制加剧脑损伤：

- **微血管堵塞与无复流**：中性粒细胞在毛细血管内黏附、聚集，形成“中性粒细胞栓子”，阻碍红细胞通过，导致微循环障碍和梗死扩大（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。
- **血脑屏障破坏**：中性粒细胞释放的ROS、MMPs和NETs可直接损伤内皮细胞和基底膜，增加血脑屏障通透性，导致水肿和出血性转化（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)；[Levinson et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/surgery/articles/10.3389/fsurg.2025.1501359/full)）。
- **促血栓形成**：中性粒细胞通过释放NETs为血小板黏附提供支架，促进血栓扩大和免疫血栓形成（[He et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2025.1641985/full)）。

动物实验中，中性粒细胞耗竭可减少梗死体积、水肿和出血性转化，这进一步证实了急性期中性粒细胞的致病作用（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。

### 2.2 慢性期：修复与炎症衰老

在缺血后5–7天，中性粒细胞表型逐渐从促炎的N1型向抗炎的N2型转变。N2型中性粒细胞表达CD206、ARG1、MMP9和YM-1，分泌TGFβ、IL-10、CCL2、VEGF等抗炎和促血管生成因子，参与组织重塑和侧支循环建立（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。然而，在老龄个体中，中性粒细胞呈现“炎症衰老”（inflammaging）特征：循环中性粒细胞高表达CXCR1、CXCL1和CXCL12，低表达CXCR4和CD44，导致其清除减少、促炎微环境持续存在（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)；[Lu et al., 2023](https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/441c/285ef1f44d4489fc055f4a715e3c2151889a.pdf)）。单细胞RNA测序进一步发现，老龄小鼠外周血中存在CD62L低表达的非典型中性粒细胞亚群，其高表达Cxcl3，与更差的卒中结局相关（[Mei et al., 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2026.1784660/full)）。

| 阶段 | 时间窗 | 主要事件 | 关键参考文献 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 超急性期 | 0–6小时 | 循环中性粒细胞增多，开始向脑实质迁移 | [Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full) |
| 急性期 | 6小时–3天 | 中性粒细胞浸润达峰，NETs形成，血脑屏障破坏 | [Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)；[He et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2025.1641985/full) |
| 亚急性/慢性期 | 5–15天 | N2型中性粒细胞出现，NETs持续存在，修复与血管新生 | [Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full) |

---

## 3. 中性粒细胞亚群异质性：N1/N2范式与单细胞图谱

### 3.1 N1/N2极化及其调控

中性粒细胞的极化受局部细胞因子微环境影响。干扰素β（IFNβ）、干扰素γ（IFNγ）和IL-12诱导N1型极化，而IL-10、TGFβ、IL-13和IL-4诱导N2型极化（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。形态学上，N1型中性粒细胞具有高度分叶的细胞核，而N2型则呈带状或环形核，反映其成熟度差异（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。

Toll样受体4（TLR4）信号在极化调控中具有关键作用。TLR4缺陷可增加N2型中性粒细胞数量并产生神经保护效应，但这种保护作用依赖于中性粒细胞的存在——在TLR4缺失背景下再耗竭中性粒细胞反而会加重脑损伤（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。这说明中性粒细胞在特定微环境中也可发挥保护功能。

| 特征 | N1型 | N2型 |
|---|---|---|
| 诱导因子 | IFNβ、IFNγ、IL-12 | IL-10、TGFβ、IL-13、IL-4 |
| 细胞核形态 | 高度分叶（成熟） | 带状/环形（未成熟） |
| 分泌分子 | IL-1β、TNFα、IFNγ、NO、ROS | TGFβ、IL-10、VEGF、CCL2 |
| 功能 | 促炎、细胞毒性 | 抗炎、组织修复、促血管生成 |
| 参考文献 | [Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)；[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full) | 同上 |

### 3.2 单细胞水平的中性粒细胞异质性

单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）进一步揭示了中性粒细胞的复杂性。在缺血后脑组织中，已鉴定出4个中性粒细胞亚群，其中最成熟的亚群（neutrophil_0）高表达Cxcl1；在外周血中则鉴定出6个亚群，其中年龄相关的非典型中性粒细胞可加重卒中损伤（[Mei et al., 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2026.1784660/full)）。此外，缺血性卒中患者外周血中具有反向跨内皮迁移表型（CD54high CXCR1low）的中性粒细胞亚群显著扩增，该亚群与疾病严重程度、全身炎症和血脑屏障破坏相关（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。

这些发现表明，中性粒细胞并非均一的群体，而是由多个功能不同的亚群组成。仅以“中性粒细胞总数”作为预后指标可能掩盖了亚群水平的差异。

---

## 4. 关键分子机制：PKM2、CD39、CXCR4与NETs

### 4.1 PKM2/STAT3通路驱动中性粒细胞过度活化

丙酮酸激酶M2（PKM2）是糖酵解的关键酶，也是系统性炎症的调节因子。研究发现，缺血性卒中后人类和小鼠中性粒细胞中核PKM2表达上调。髓系特异性敲除PKM2可减少外周中性粒细胞的炎症反应和NETs形成，并在野生型和高脂血症小鼠模型中均减少梗死体积、改善长期感觉运动功能恢复。机制上，PKM2通过促进STAT3磷酸化驱动中性粒细胞过度活化；小分子抑制PKM2核转位同样可减轻中性粒细胞过度活化并改善卒中结局（[Dhanesha et al., 2021](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/doi/10.1182/blood.2021012322/476940/PKM2-promotes-neutrophil-activation-and-cerebral)）。这为中性粒细胞靶向治疗提供了新的分子靶点。

### 4.2 CD39与CXCR4：中性粒细胞迁移的调控节点

中性粒细胞表面的CD39（一种细胞外ATP酶）可抑制中性粒细胞向脑实质的侵袭，并显著减少卒中后的行为缺陷，提示CD39具有神经保护作用（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。CXCR4信号则主要调控骨髓中性粒细胞的滞留与释放。CXCR4与骨髓基质细胞表达的CXCL12结合，使中性粒细胞保留在骨髓中；而G-CSF等刺激可下调SDF-1、上调KC和Groβ，促进中性粒细胞释放入血。因此，调控CXCR4信号的药物可能有效控制卒中后中性粒细胞的全身动员（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。

### 4.3 NETs：从抗菌到促炎、促血栓的“双刃剑”

NETs是由去浓缩染色质、组蛋白和抗菌蛋白组成的网状结构。在缺血性卒中中，NETs在脑组织和血栓中显著升高，并与卒中严重程度和不良临床结局相关（[He et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2025.1641985/full)）。在血管衰老背景下，过度的NETs释放可驱动内皮功能障碍、炎症性衰老和血管重塑，参与高血压、动脉粥样硬化、缺血性卒中甚至阿尔茨海默病的病理过程；调节NETs可保护内皮完整性并改善预后（[Frontiers in Immunology, 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2025.1657938/full)）。

然而，血液中的NETs标志物（如cfDNA、MPO-组蛋白复合物、DNase活性）可能无法可靠反映血栓内NETs的实际含量，这限制了其作为血栓成分和预后预测生物标志物的应用（[Baumann et al., 2024](https://edoc.unibas.ch/entities/publication/1320d1ba-8056-4db5-b16d-48ad02cf060f)）。

---

## 5. 中性粒细胞亚群与其他细胞的相互作用：从网络到结局

### 5.1 NETs与巨噬细胞/小胶质细胞的双向反馈

近年研究提供了NETs与巨噬细胞在人类脑血栓中相互作用的原位证据。急性缺血性卒中患者血栓中的NETs含量与M1和M2巨噬细胞密度均相关，且患者来源的巨噬细胞对NETs的降解能力存在差异（[Zang et al., 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0329764)）。既往研究已表明，NETs可“授权”巨噬细胞产生细胞因子（Warnatsch et al., 2015），而M1/M2巨噬细胞的分泌组可减少NETs释放（Manda-Handzlik et al., 2023），提示存在一个NETs-巨噬细胞正反馈环路（[Zang et al., 2025](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0329764)；[Ardic & Dinc, 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1752471/full)）。

小胶质细胞作为中枢神经系统的常驻免疫细胞，同样能够感知NETs成分，并通过模式识别受体、炎症小体、趋化因子网络和细胞因子环路参与这一自放大炎症过程（[Ardic & Dinc, 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1752471/full)）。小胶质细胞还与神经元、星形胶质细胞和微血管内皮细胞形成复杂的通讯网络，M2型小胶质细胞来源的细胞外囊泡可抑制星形胶质细胞增殖、减少胶质瘢痕形成，从而促进恢复（[Zhang et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cellular-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fncel.2022.889442/full)）。

### 5.2 中性粒细胞与单核细胞、T细胞的协同

中性粒细胞可促进单核细胞募集。在缺血后，单核细胞在4–6小时后开始黏附于血管壁并进入缺血区，其活性在3–7天达到高峰（[Chen et al., 2021](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.692061/full)）。单细胞测序还揭示了T细胞在缺血后脑组织中的双重作用：部分T细胞亚群驱动炎症和缺血损伤，另一些则具有神经保护作用（[Mei et al., 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2026.1784660/full)）。中性粒细胞可能通过释放趋化因子和NETs影响T细胞极化，但目前相关证据仍有限。

### 5.3 中性粒细胞与侧支循环

中性粒细胞亚群对侧支循环的建立具有双向调节作用。缺血后，中性粒细胞浸润和有害亚群在侧支血管中的表达可加重卒中致病性，即使患者入院时侧支状态良好；而促血管生成的N2型中性粒细胞则可在恢复期增强侧支生长（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。这提示中性粒细胞亚群构成可能是影响侧支重塑和最终临床结局的重要变量。

---

## 6. 临床结局预测：从生物标志物到亚群导向模型

### 6.1 中性粒细胞计数与NLR

多项研究表明，入院时中性粒细胞计数升高与更大的梗死体积和更差的临床结局相关。中性粒细胞/淋巴细胞比值（NLR）已被提出作为独立于年龄和再通状态的炎症反应及预后标志物（[Bui et al., 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/aging-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnagi.2022.1041333/full)）。然而，NLR仅反映总量，无法区分N1/N2或有害/保护亚群。

### 6.2 NETs与血栓特征

血栓内NETs含量与临床结局相关。Lapostolle等的研究显示，缺血性卒中血栓中的NETs与不良临床结局相关（转引自[He et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2025.1641985/full)）。但血液NETs标志物与血栓NETs含量之间的关联较弱，提示仅凭血液标志物难以准确预测血栓成分和结局（[Baumann et al., 2024](https://edoc.unibas.ch/entities/publication/1320d1ba-8056-4db5-b16d-48ad02cf060f)）。

### 6.3 血管危险因素与神经退行性结局

从更广的临床结局来看，血管危险因素可能通过中性粒细胞/NETs轴驱动神经退行性改变。一项针对美国黑人的研究发现，中年期共病高血压和糖尿病与11年内神经丝轻链（NfL）水平升高显著相关，但与p-Tau181无关，提示其主要贡献是血管性痴呆而非阿尔茨海默病病理（[BlackDoctor Pro, 2025](https://blackdoctor.pro/hypertension-diabetes-dementia)）。结合NETs在血管衰老和动脉粥样硬化中的作用（[Frontiers in Immunology, 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2025.1657938/full)），可以推测，长期血管危险因素可能通过慢性中性粒细胞活化和NETs释放，加速血管损伤和认知功能下降。

### 6.4 亚群导向的结局预测模型

综合上述证据，可以构建一个亚群导向的临床结局预测模型：

- **急性期**：若骨髓释放以CXCR2+成熟中性粒细胞为主，且局部微环境富含IFNγ/IL-12，则N1/NET轴占优，导致血脑屏障破坏、微血管无复流和血栓扩大，最终表现为大梗死体积和不良神经功能结局。
- **恢复期**：若IL-10/TGFβ占优，N2/CD39high亚群增多，则促进修复性血管生成和侧支循环建立，有利于功能恢复。
- **慢性期**：若NETs持续存在并与巨噬细胞/小胶质细胞形成正反馈，则推动血管衰老和神经退行性改变，可能表现为血管性认知障碍；若NETs被有效清除，巨噬细胞向M2极化，则有助于组织修复和认知保留。

这一模型仍需前瞻性队列和单细胞水平验证，但它为理解中性粒细胞异质性如何导向不同临床结局提供了框架。

---

## 7. 未来研究方向

### 7.1 构建多时间点、多组织的单细胞时空图谱

目前scRNA-seq研究多为单时间点、单组织取样。未来需要整合脑、血液、骨髓和侧支血管的多时间点数据，结合空间转录组学，绘制中性粒细胞亚群的动态演变图谱，并明确其与年龄、性别和共病的关系（[Mei et al., 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2026.1784660/full)）。

### 7.2 开发可靠的NETs生物标志物

血液cfDNA、MPO-组蛋白复合物等标志物不能可靠反映血栓内NETs含量。未来需要开发新的成像或液体活检方法，例如靶向NETs的分子影像探针，或结合血栓蛋白质组学筛选更具特异性的标志物（[Baumann et al., 2024](https://edoc.unibas.ch/entities/publication/1320d1ba-8056-4db5-b16d-48ad02cf060f)）。

### 7.3 推进亚群靶向和时序特异性干预

全局性中性粒细胞耗竭在临床上不可行，且可能增加感染风险。未来应聚焦于：

- **急性期**：抑制PKM2核转位、PAD4介导的NETosis、N1极化相关信号（如TLR4/STAT3）。
- **恢复期**：增强CD39表达、促进N2极化、应用DNase I清除NETs。
- **反馈环干预**：阻断NETs-巨噬细胞/小胶质细胞正反馈，例如通过靶向NETs感应受体或炎症小体通路（[Ardic & Dinc, 2026](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1752471/full)；[Dhanesha et al., 2021](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/doi/10.1182/blood.2021012322/476940/PKM2-promotes-neutrophil-activation-and-cerebral)；[He et al., 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2025.1641985/full)）。

### 7.4 将血管危险因素管理纳入神经保护策略

高血压和糖尿病等血管危险因素不仅是卒中的病因，也可能通过慢性炎症和NETs机制加速神经退行性改变。未来研究应评估强化血压和血糖控制能否降低NfL等神经退行性标志物水平，并改善长期认知结局（[BlackDoctor Pro, 2025](https://blackdoctor.pro/hypertension-diabetes-dementia)；[Frontiers in Immunology, 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2025.1657938/full)）。

---

## 8. 结论

中性粒细胞在脑缺血中的角色不是单一的“致病”或“保护”，而是一个由时间、微环境、年龄和共病共同决定的动态系统。急性期N1/NET轴主导的过度炎症反应是导致血脑屏障破坏、微循环障碍和不良预后的关键；慢性期N2/修复轴和NETs清除能力则决定组织修复和认知保留的程度。笔者认为，未来最有前景的策略是“亚群靶向”与“时序调控”相结合：在急性期抑制PKM2/NETs/N1通路，在恢复期增强CD39/N2/修复通路，并通过调控NETs-巨噬细胞/小胶质细胞反馈环来打破炎症恶性循环。同时，积极管理高血压和糖尿病等血管危险因素，可能是预防血管性痴呆的最有效手段之一。这一领域正从“中性粒细胞有害”的简单范式，转向“亚群动态平衡决定结局”的精准医学范式。
