.</think># From Mean-Variance to Machine Learning: A Comparative Synthesis of Asset Allocation Models and the Case for a Hybrid Black-Litterman-ML Framework

## 1. Introduction

The application of machine learning (ML) to asset allocation has grown from a niche quantitative technique into a mainstream FinTech practice. Classic models such as Mean-Variance Optimization (MVO) and Black-Litterman (BL) remain foundational, while deep learning and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate return forecasts and even end-to-end portfolio policies. Each approach has distinct strengths and weaknesses, particularly in how it measures risk, predicts returns, and translates those inputs into allocations. This report synthesizes research across these branches and argues that the most promising path toward a general-purpose framework is not to replace classical models with deep learning, but to embed ML-generated views and adaptive confidence calibration inside a Bayesian Black-Litterman core, augmented by robust covariance estimation and tail-risk-aware optimization.

## 2. Foundational Models: Mean-Variance and Black-Litterman

### 2.1 Mean-Variance Optimization

Modern portfolio theory begins with Markowitz's MVO, which assumes that investors optimize the trade-off between expected return and variance. The model requires explicit expected return estimates for every asset and a covariance matrix, then solves for weights that maximize return for a given risk level. Its theoretical elegance, however, is undermined by practical fragility. MVO is extremely sensitive to small changes in return assumptions; small estimation errors can produce wildly different, concentrated portfolios ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). It also assumes returns are normally distributed, an assumption that often fails in real markets where fat tails and correlation spikes occur during crises ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). The result is that MVO is often described as an "error maximizer" rather than a practical allocation tool ([AL Capital Advisory, 2026](https://alcapitaladvisory.com/research/frameworks/black-litterman.html)).

### 2.2 Black-Litterman as a Bayesian Correction

The Black-Litterman model, developed by Fischer Black and Robert Litterman at Goldman Sachs, was designed to address MVO's instability. It starts from market equilibrium returns derived by reverse-optimizing the market portfolio:

$$\Pi = \lambda \Sigma w_{mkt}$$

where $\Pi$ is the vector of implied equilibrium excess returns, $\lambda$ is the risk aversion coefficient, $\Sigma$ is the covariance matrix, and $w_{mkt}$ is the market-capitalization weight vector ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). These equilibrium returns serve as a Bayesian prior. Investor views are then expressed through a pick matrix $P$, a view vector $Q$, and a diagonal uncertainty matrix $\Omega$. The posterior expected returns are computed as:

$$E(R) = \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1} + P^\top\Omega^{-1}P\right]^{-1} \left[(\tau\Sigma)^{-1}\Pi + P^\top\Omega^{-1}Q\right]$$

([PyPortfolioOpt, n.d.](https://pyportfolioopt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/BlackLitterman.html)).

The BL model produces more stable and diversified portfolios than raw MVO because it anchors allocations to market equilibrium and only tilts toward views in proportion to their confidence ([Hyperbots, n.d.](https://www.hyperbots.com/glossary/black-litterman-model)). It also gracefully degrades: with no views, the posterior returns equal the equilibrium prior, and unconstrained MVO recovers the market portfolio ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)).

However, BL is not a replacement for MVO. It is an input framework: the posterior excess returns are fed into a constrained optimizer to produce final weights ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). Its limitations include subjective view specification, difficult calibration of $\Omega$ and $\tau$, and the assumption of normally distributed returns with a stable covariance matrix ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model); [Hudson & Thames, n.d.](https://hudsonthames.org/bayesian-portfolio-optimisation-the-black-litterman-model)).

## 3. Machine Learning and Deep Learning in Asset Allocation

### 3.1 ML-Generated Views for Black-Litterman

A central challenge in BL is view generation. Traditional implementations rely on subjective analyst forecasts, which introduces bias. Machine learning offers a data-driven alternative. One hybrid approach uses ARMA-GARCH models to predict stock indicators and Support Vector Regression (SVR) to generate return forecasts, which are then fed into the BL model to compute optimal portfolio weights; this was tested on the Dow Jones Index ([Rong, n.d.](https://github.com/Yebei-Rong/A-Hybrid-Approach-for-Generating-Investor-Views-in-Black-Litterman-Model)). Similarly, GARCH-family models have been used to quantify view vectors for industry asset allocation, with investor sentiment indices mapped to confidence levels through probability distributions ([Pang, 2021](https://www.kygl.net.cn/EN/abstract/abstract22461.shtml)). More advanced work combines copula functions with GARCH to construct a novel view error matrix, capturing correlations that standard diagonal $\Omega$ matrices ignore; this approach outperformed He-Litterman and Idzorek calibrations in Sharpe ratio terms ([Deng, Zhou, & Cao, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/compec/v66y2025i4d10.1007_s10614-024-10815-x.html)).

### 3.2 LLM-Based Return Forecasts and Views

Large language models represent the newest frontier in view generation. A 2025 study proposes a systematic framework to translate LLM return forecasts and predictive uncertainty into BL investor views and confidence levels, addressing the key challenge of view generation ([RePEc, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/p/arx/papers/2504.14345.html)). Empirical backtests on S&P 500 constituents show that portfolios driven by top-performing LLMs significantly outperform traditional baselines in both absolute and risk-adjusted terms ([RePEc, 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/p/arx/papers/2504.14345.html)). LLMs can generate expected return views from historical prices and company metadata, with uncertainty quantified via prediction variance ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)). However, different LLMs exhibit varying levels of predictive optimism and confidence stability, which significantly impacts BL portfolio performance ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)).

A particularly striking result comes from a multi-LLM sentiment aggregation approach. By aggregating sentiment scores from multiple finance-domain fine-tuned LLMs using an LSTM network to form a Meta-LLM sentiment score, and incorporating it as views in the BL model, the strategy achieved an annualized return of 31.22% versus 24.57% for the market cap-weighted portfolio, with a Sharpe ratio of 3.02 ([Business Perspectives, n.d.](https://businessperspectives.org/journals/investment-management-and-financial-innovations/issue-493/enhancing-portfolio-optimization-with-multi-llm-sentiment-aggregation-a-black-litterman-integration-approach)).

### 3.3 Deep Learning and Reinforcement Learning

Beyond view generation, deep learning and reinforcement learning (RL) have been applied directly to portfolio construction. One study used ML and deep learning models to build return forecasts, with a trained DQN agent selecting the optimal prediction among models to construct the BL view matrix. The BL approach showed lower variance and smoother returns than classical Markowitz, though it underperformed in the early testing period and outperformed in more volatile periods ([Vasilevich & Byers, n.d.](https://www.opastpublishers.com/open-access-articles/blacklitterman-portfolio-optimization-using-machinelearning-deep-learning-and-reinforcement-learning-algorithms-10301.html)). This highlights both the potential and the risk of ML-driven allocation: predictive power may be regime-dependent.

## 4. Core Differences Across Models

The table below summarizes the fundamental differences in risk measurement, return prediction, and allocation mechanism.

| Dimension | Mean-Variance (MVO) | Black-Litterman (BL) | ML/LLM-Driven BL | Deep Learning / RL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Risk measurement** | Variance/covariance of historical returns | Posterior covariance = $\Sigma + V$, where $V$ captures estimation uncertainty | Same as BL, but with dynamic volatility models (GARCH, DCC, copula) | Learned state-dependent risk, often opaque |
| **Return prediction** | Historical or subjective expected returns | Market equilibrium prior blended with investor views | ML/LLM forecasts as views, with uncertainty from prediction variance | Non-linear learned forecasts, often end-to-end |
| **Asset allocation** | Direct quadratic optimization | Posterior returns fed into constrained MVO | Same as BL, with ML-generated views and confidence | End-to-end policy or RL agent selecting models |
| **Interpretability** | High | Moderate | Moderate | Low |
| **Key strength** | Theoretical foundation | Stability, diversification, view integration | Reduces subjectivity in views; can capture complex signals | Handles non-linear relationships |
| **Key limitation** | Input sensitivity, normality assumption | Subjective views, $\Omega$/$\tau$ calibration, normality assumption | Model risk, data-mining bias, LLM optimism variance | Poor interpretability, overfitting, regime dependence |

### 4.1 Risk Measurement

MVO treats risk as variance, which is only appropriate for normally distributed returns. BL improves on this by adding a posterior covariance that includes uncertainty about the expected return estimates themselves ([PyPortfolioOpt, n.d.](https://pyportfolioopt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/BlackLitterman.html)). However, both models assume a stable covariance matrix, which can understate risk during crises when correlations spike and return distributions exhibit fat tails ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). Dynamic extensions using DCC or copula-GARCH models address this by allowing time-varying correlations and volatility ([Harris, Stoja, & Tan, 2017](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/94044423/Dynamic_Black_Litterman.pdf); [Deng et al., 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/compec/v66y2025i4d10.1007_s10614-024-10815-x.html)). Deep learning models can in principle learn non-linear risk dependencies, but their risk estimates are often not transparent or easily auditable.

### 4.2 Return Prediction

MVO requires explicit return estimates for every asset, which is its Achilles' heel. BL replaces this with equilibrium returns derived from market prices, making it forward-looking and less reliant on historical averages ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). ML and LLM approaches generate views from data, reducing the subjectivity of human forecasts. For example, LLMs can produce expected return views from historical prices and metadata, with uncertainty quantified via prediction variance ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)). However, the quality of these views depends heavily on the model's predictive optimism and stability, which varies across LLMs ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)).

### 4.3 Asset Allocation

MVO directly optimizes weights. BL produces posterior returns that must be fed into an optimizer; it does not itself generate final weights ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). ML-driven BL follows the same pipeline, with the view vector and confidence matrix generated by algorithms. Deep RL approaches can bypass the explicit optimization step entirely, learning a policy that maps market states to portfolio weights. While this can capture complex dynamics, it sacrifices interpretability and may overfit to historical regimes.

## 5. Toward a General-Purpose Hybrid Framework

The research strongly suggests that the strengths of these models are complementary. A general-purpose framework should combine the equilibrium anchor of BL, the predictive power of ML/LLMs, and the robustness of modern covariance and tail-risk techniques.

### 5.1 Use ML/LLMs to Generate Views and Confidence

The most direct way to reduce BL's subjectivity is to use ML models to generate both the view vector $Q$ and the uncertainty matrix $\Omega$. LLMs can generate return forecasts from unstructured data, and their prediction variance can serve as a natural confidence measure ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)). This addresses the "no guidance on view generation" limitation of BL ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)). Hybrid approaches using ARMA-GARCH and SVR have already demonstrated the feasibility of this pipeline on the Dow Jones Index ([Rong, n.d.](https://github.com/Yebei-Rong/A-Hybrid-Approach-for-Generating-Investor-Views-in-Black-Litterman-Model)).

### 5.2 Fix Omega Calibration: The Tau Cancellation Problem

A critical technical issue is the standard He-Litterman calibration of $\Omega$:

$$\Omega = \tau \cdot P \Sigma P^\top$$

This calibration can suffer from a tau cancellation issue that prevents view confidence from genuinely moving expected returns. Practitioners need an independently calibrated confidence multiplier for $\Omega$ so that model accuracy affects expected returns rather than just covariances ([Pomorski, n.d.](https://piotrpomorski.substack.com/p/tactical-asset-allocation-with-ml)). Several solutions exist:

- **Idzorek's confidence-level method**: The analyst specifies intuitive percentage confidence levels (e.g., 70% confidence), and the model back-solves for the corresponding $\Omega$ entries. This is the most widely adopted practical calibration ([AL Capital Advisory, 2026](https://alcapitaladvisory.com/research/frameworks/black-litterman.html)).
- **Machine-learning-based dynamic $\Omega$**: Systematic systems can monitor the real-time accuracy of views and programmatically tighten or expand $\Omega$ based on historical hit rates ([Picture Perfect Portfolios, n.d.](https://pictureperfectportfolios.com/breaking-down-the-black-litterman-model-for-optimal-asset-allocation)).
- **Copula-GARCH view error matrix**: Combining GARCH forecasted volatility with copula-based correlations produces a view error matrix that outperforms He-Litterman and Idzorek methods in Sharpe ratio terms ([Deng et al., 2025](https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/compec/v66y2025i4d10.1007_s10614-024-10815-x.html)).

### 5.3 Generalize Tau and Covariance Estimation

The scalar $\tau$ in BL is difficult to calibrate and introduces rigidity. A proposed generalization replaces $\tau$ with asset-specific uncertainty parameters derived from regression $R^2$ or judgmental confidence intervals, while still permitting the original model as a special case ([OTH Working Paper, n.d.](https://www.oth-aw.de/files/oth-aw/Aktuelles/Veroeffentlichungen/WEN-Diskussionspapier/WEN-DPs-PDF/DP68.pdf)). Similarly, the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ should not be a raw historical sample covariance. Shrinkage estimators like Ledoit-Wolf are essential for stability, especially with 10+ assets ([AL Capital Advisory, 2026](https://alcapitaladvisory.com/research/frameworks/black-litterman.html)). Dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) models have been shown to improve BL portfolio performance by capturing time-varying correlations ([Harris et al., 2017](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/94044423/Dynamic_Black_Litterman.pdf)).

### 5.4 Incorporate Tail Risk and Non-Normality

Both MVO and BL assume normality, which is problematic during market crises. Extensions such as Meucci's five-step recipe for inputting views on non-normal markets highlight the need to move beyond normality ([Hudson & Thames, n.d.](https://hudsonthames.org/bayesian-portfolio-optimisation-the-black-litterman-model)). Dynamic BL portfolios constructed using reward-to-VaR and reward-to-CVaR ratios outperform benchmarks and lead to more diversified portfolios than standard mean-variance portfolios ([Harris et al., 2017](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/94044423/Dynamic_Black_Litterman.pdf)). A practical framework should therefore feed BL posterior returns into a constrained optimizer that can minimize CVaR or apply tail-risk constraints, rather than relying solely on variance.

### 5.5 Proposed Architecture

Based on the evidence, a robust general-purpose framework would be modular:

1. **Data layer**: Historical prices, alternative data, sentiment, and company metadata.
2. **View generation**: LLMs or ML models produce return forecasts $Q$ and uncertainty estimates (e.g., prediction variance).
3. **Prior construction**: Reverse optimization using a robust covariance matrix (Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage or DCC).
4. **Bayesian fusion**: BL posterior returns with asset-specific $\tau$ and an independently calibrated $\Omega$ (Idzorek or ML-based dynamic confidence).
5. **Optimization**: Constrained MVO or CVaR optimization to produce final weights.
6. **Feedback loop**: Track view accuracy over time and recalibrate $\Omega$ accordingly.

This architecture preserves the interpretability and equilibrium anchor of BL while leveraging ML's predictive power. It also addresses the key limitations identified in the literature: subjective views, tau cancellation, covariance instability, and normality assumptions.

## 6. Challenges and Open Problems

No hybrid framework is a panacea. The research highlights several persistent challenges:

- **Model complexity can obscure poor assumptions**: A BL portfolio built on a flawed covariance matrix or poorly calibrated views may underperform simpler approaches like equal-weight or risk parity ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)).
- **LLM optimism and stability vary**: Different LLMs exhibit varying levels of predictive optimism and confidence stability, which significantly impacts BL portfolio performance ([ICLR, 2025](https://iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33834)). Model selection and ensemble methods are therefore critical.
- **Data-mining bias and turnover**: ML-driven strategies risk overfitting and high transaction costs, especially in taxable accounts ([Picture Perfect Portfolios, n.d.](https://pictureperfectportfolios.com/breaking-down-the-black-litterman-model-for-optimal-asset-allocation)).
- **Confidence calibration remains subjective**: There is no single objectively correct method for setting $\Omega$; different analysts with the same views but different confidence levels will produce different portfolios ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)).
- **Single-period framework**: Like standard MVO, BL is a single-period model and does not account for multi-period dynamics, rebalancing costs, or changing horizons ([Ryan O'Connell, CFA, 2026](https://ryanoconnellfinance.com/black-litterman-model)).

## 7. Conclusion

The core differences between MVO, BL, and deep learning models lie in how they measure risk, generate return expectations, and translate those into allocations. MVO is theoretically elegant but practically fragile. BL provides a Bayesian anchor that stabilizes portfolios and incorporates views, but it depends on subjective inputs and difficult-to-calibrate confidence parameters. Deep learning and LLMs can generate rich, non-linear forecasts and reduce subjectivity, but they suffer from poor interpretability and regime dependence.

The most promising direction is not to choose between these paradigms, but to combine them. A hybrid framework that uses ML/LLMs to generate views and confidence, robust covariance models to capture time-varying risk, BL to blend equilibrium with views, and constrained optimization with tail-risk awareness offers the best balance of stability, predictive power, and interpretability. The empirical evidence—from LLM-driven BL outperforming baselines to Meta-LLM sentiment achieving a 3.02 Sharpe ratio—supports this synthesis. However, practitioners must remain vigilant about calibration, model selection, and the inherent subjectivity of confidence. A general-purpose framework is achievable, but it requires disciplined modular design and continuous feedback, not a single black-box model.

# Prometheus 高流失率（Series Churn）的影响、系统性解决方案与云厂商方案综述

## 摘要

Prometheus 的时间序列流失（series churn）——即标签组合因工作负载重建、自动扩缩容、短生命周期任务等原因被频繁创建与废弃的现象——是云原生监控体系中最具破坏性且最容易被低估的结构性问题之一。本报告基于 2026 年的多层级研究资料，系统梳理了高流失率对内存、查询性能、成本与可用性的影响路径，归纳了从"发现—治理—架构重构"三个层次递进的系统性解决方案，并对比了 AWS、Google Cloud、Azure 三大云厂商托管 Prometheus 服务的现有应对能力。研究发现：高流失率本质上是"标签设计问题"与"存储架构问题"的叠加；在治理层面，指标重标记（relabeling）、录制规则（recording rules）与原生直方图（native histograms）构成了成本最低的干预手段；在架构层面，远程写入（remote write）加集中式多租户后端（Mimir、Thanos、Cortex）是横向扩展的既定路径；而三大云厂商已分别通过配额监控、标签级主动系列上限、原生直方图计量优惠及长期保留内嵌等手段，将流失率治理内置为托管服务能力。

---

## 1. 引言：高流失率的定义与本质

Prometheus 的时间序列由"指标名 + 标签集合"唯一标识，每出现一个新的标签组合即创建一条新序列。**高流失率（high churn rate）** 指的是序列被创建与废弃的速率远高于稳定速率的现象——即使总流量保持不变，只要部署频繁重建 Pod、自动扩缩容持续触发、短生命周期任务反复启停，head 区的活跃序列数就会持续攀升。Last9 的技术分析明确指出："Churn matters as much as scale. Deployments that recreate pods, autoscaling, and short-lived jobs all retire old label sets and create new ones, so head series climb even when traffic is flat."（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。流失率与高基数（high cardinality）是两个相互关联但不同的维度：高基数描述的是某一时刻标签组合的广度，而高流失率描述的是标签组合随时间的更替速度。两者叠加时，监控系统的压力呈乘法效应。

Kubernetes 环境是流失率的放大器。Grafana Labs 的工程团队指出，Kubernetes 中每个指标都携带 pod、namespace、instance 标签，"一百个 Pod 被一个 Prometheus 实例抓取，一个计数器在添加任何应用标签之前就已经变成了一百条序列"（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。容器 ID、Pod UID、提交 SHA 等无界标签值一旦被纳入标签，每次重建都会铸造全新序列。

## 2. 高流失率的影响

### 2.1 内存与计算资源侵蚀

Prometheus 的索引式存储结构将标签倒排索引与时间序列位图保存在内存中，序列数量直接决定内存占用。每条活跃序列在 head 区块中大约消耗 **1 至 3 KiB**，一台 16 GB 内存的实例仅能舒适运行约数百万条活跃序列（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。高流失率意味着旧序列尚未从内存中完全释放、新序列已持续涌入，导致 head 区序列数在高位徘徊，内存、CPU、磁盘 I/O 全面承压，查询延迟随之恶化。

### 2.2 成本失控

流失率直接转化为账单增长。Grafana Labs 观察到，"指标基数（指标与标签的笛卡尔积）的增长速度已经超过了被监控应用与基础设施的扩张速度"，这是企业观测成本失控的首要原因（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。在托管服务场景中，成本按样本数计量——AWS 按摄入样本数分级计费（[AWS Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/prometheus/pricing)），GCP 按每百万样本 $0.060 起计费（[Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/managed-prometheus)），Azure 按摄入与查询样本计费（[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/metrics/prometheus-metrics-overview)）。流失率越高，被计费的有效样本中"一次性序列"的占比越大，而这类数据几乎不产生长期查询价值。

### 2.3 可用性风险

Last9 强调了一个常被忽视的事实："高基数同时也是预算和可用性问题，而不仅仅是性能问题。当实例触及内存上限时，团队被迫丢弃指标或缩短保留期，而你在排障时最需要的数据恰恰是最先消失的数据。"（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。这意味着流失率问题会在最关键的故障时刻反噬排障能力。

### 2.4 查询性能退化

高流失率导致倒排索引膨胀，查询需要扫描的位图范围扩大。Grafana 官方博客给出的诊断指标是"将 `prometheus_tsdb_head_series` 的持续攀升视为真正的警报，并围绕活跃序列而非每秒样本数做容量规划"（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。

## 3. 根因分析

| 根因类别 | 具体表现 | 典型来源 |
|---------|---------|---------|
| 无界标签 | user_id、session_id、device_id、原始 URL 路径、容器 ID | 应用埋点设计缺陷（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)） |
| 基础设施噪音 | Node exporter 约 500 条序列、MySQL exporter 约 1000 条序列，且并非全部有价值 | 导出器过度暴露（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)） |
| 经典直方图桶爆炸 | 20 桶直方图 = 22 条序列/标签集（桶 + _sum + _count） | 直方图精度配置不当（[AWS Cloud Operations Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/introducing-native-histogram-support-in-amazon-managed-service-for-prometheus)） |
| 运维方式导致的序列更替 | 频繁发布、HPA 扩缩容、短任务 | Kubernetes 原生特性（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)） |

Groundcover 的实践指南补充了一个关键判断标准："避免在指标中使用 user_id、request_id、session_id、pod UID 或任意错误消息等标签；将高基数细节放入日志和追踪，指标只保留应当保持廉价和快速的聚合结果。"（[groundcover, 2026](https://www.groundcover.com/learn/observability/prometheus-cardinality)）

## 4. 系统性解决方案

### 4.1 第一层：发现与定位

在治理之前必须先量化问题。Prometheus 提供了三层发现工具：

- **TSDB Status 端点**：直接暴露 head 序列数、每个指标的序列占比；
- **PromQL 聚合查询**：`count({__name__=~".+"}) by (__name__)` 找出序列数最高的指标；`topk(10, count by (__name__, job)({__name__=~".+"}))` 定位产生高基数指标的 Job（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）；
- **Grafana 官方仪表盘**：导入 Prometheus Stats（ID: 1860）或 Prometheus 2.0 Stats（ID: 3662）可视化全量序列数（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。

Grafana Cloud 的基数管理仪表盘进一步将指标按"高价值/高成本"四象限分类，优先处理"高成本但未被任何仪表盘、告警或录制规则引用"的指标；Mimirtool 可自动识别未使用指标并生成 JSON 清单（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。

### 4.2 第二层：抓取侧治理（成本最低的干预）

Last9 给出的操作原则是"自上而下，取 tsdb check 中最差的两三个指标，应用最便宜的修复"——依次为重标记、聚合、抓取级护栏（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。

**指标重标记（metric_relabel_configs）** 是最直接的削减手段。典型配置如下：

```yaml
metric_relabel_configs:
- source_labels: [__name__, le]
  regex: "http_request_duration_seconds_bucket;(0.005|0.01|0.025)"
  action: drop
```

但需注意：删除标签可能导致序列合并冲突，Prometheus 会因时间戳冲突而丢弃重复数据点，因此需先评估影响（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。

**录制规则（recording rules）** 用于无法直接删标签的场景：先聚合再存储，保留聚合值、丢弃原始细粒度序列。例如 `sum by(env) (my_metric_total{})` 将 100 条带 IP 标签的序列收敛为 1 条（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。

**抓取级护栏** 包括四类可强制执行的限制（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）：

| 配置项 | 作用 | 触发后果 |
|--------|------|---------|
| `sample_limit` | 单次抓取样本数上限 | 整个抓取失败，目标 `up=0` |
| `label_limit` | 每条序列标签数上限（v2.27+） | 同上 |
| `label_name_length_limit` / `label_value_length_limit` | 标签名/值长度上限 | 同上 |
| `target_limit` | 每个 Job 发现目标数上限 | 同上 |

这些护栏是"针对坏部署的保险丝"而非调优旋钮，必须配合 `prometheus_target_scrapes_exceeded_sample_limit_total` 告警使用。

**抓取间隔调整** 是常被低估的成本杠杆：将低频指标抓取间隔从 15 秒调至 60 秒，成本可降低高达 75%（[Grafana Labs, 2022](https://grafana.com/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus-and-kubernetes)）。

### 4.3 第三层：原生直方图——结构性的桶爆炸修复

经典直方图是序列爆炸的最大单一来源之一。AWS 官方博客给出了清晰的数据对比：一个 20 桶的经典直方图需要 22 条序列（桶 + _sum + _count），而原生直方图将整个分布压缩为 **1 条序列**，对直方图密集型工作负载可减少高达 **75%** 的活跃序列数与计费样本量（[AWS Cloud Operations Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/introducing-native-histogram-support-in-amazon-managed-service-for-prometheus)）。

但原生直方图并非自动生效。Logz.io 明确警告："原生直方图不具备追溯性，现有经典直方图不会自动转换；采用需要显式启用原生直方图抓取、更新客户端库埋点，并在适用处启用 remote_write 转发——这是一项需要规划的迁移，而非升级后免费获得的能力。"（[Logz.io, 2026](https://logz.io/blog/prometheus-metrics-native-histograms)）此外，原生直方图只解决桶乘法问题，不解决高基数标签问题："过去多年在标签设计上保持纪律的团队，不应将此视为放松纪律的理由。"（[Logz.io, 2026](https://logz.io/blog/prometheus-metrics-native-histograms)）

### 4.4 第四层：架构级扩展——远程写入与集中式后端

当单实例 Prometheus 无法承载规模时，远程写入（remote write）是聚合多集群指标的标准机制。Groundcover 将其定义为"把本地监控转变为全局可观测性战略的桥梁"，核心收益包括：跨集群单一全局视图、对象存储中的长期保留、将高基数数据卸载到水平扩展后端以保护抓取端、以及混合云/多云监控（[groundcover, 2026](https://www.groundcover.com/learn/observability/prometheus-remote-write)）。

Prometheus 内嵌 TSDB 默认仅保留 15 天数据（[Greptime, 2026](https://greptime.com/tech-content/2026-06-17-prometheus-long-term-storage-options)），因此长期存储必选外部后端。2026 年的长期存储方案分为两大架构阵营（[Greptime, 2026](https://greptime.com/tech-content/2026-06-17-prometheus-long-term-storage-options)）：

| 阵营 | 代表 | 架构特征 | 适用场景 |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| Prometheus 原生栈 | Thanos、Mimir、Cortex | 扩展 CNCF 生态，对象存储 + 原生 PromQL | 保持 Prometheus 为数据源 |
| 专用数据库 | VictoriaMetrics、GreptimeDB | Remote Write 摄入，自研存储引擎 | 追求极致性能与压缩比 |

选型建议方面，Bigyan Raj Dahal 的对比分析给出了明确结论："**新部署推荐 Mimir**，因其集中式多租户特性；**Thanos 最适合为既有 Prometheus 舰队增加全局查询与长期保留**；Cortex 仅建议既有 Cortex 用户延续使用。"（[Bigyan Raj Dahal](https://www.bigyanrajdahal.com/blog/when-to-use-mimir-cortex-thanos)）Thanos 的代价是组件分散（Sidecar、Compactor、Store Gateway、Querier），跨大范围历史区间的对象存储查询延迟需要缓存与调优（[Greptime, 2026](https://greptime.com/tech-content/2026-06-17-prometheus-long-term-storage-options)）。更关键的是，**Thanos 本身不解决高基数问题**——在 2026 年的对比中，Cortex、Mimir 与 VictoriaMetrics 在高基数处理上被评为有效，而 Prometheus 与 Thanos 在该维度被标记为红色（[Oodle AI Blog](https://blog.oodle.ai/scaling-prometheus-from-single-node-to-enterprise-grade-observability)）。

**最经济的扩展策略**是先削减基数、再增加存储："先丢弃未使用的标签，采用 Prometheus 3 原生直方图（将指数桶直方图存储为单条序列而非多条桶序列），然后再添加远程存储。"（[Oodle AI Blog](https://blog.oodle.ai/scaling-prometheus-from-single-node-to-enterprise-grade-observability)）

## 5. 云厂商现有方案对比

三大云厂商均已将流失率治理能力内置到托管 Prometheus 服务中，但实现路径与侧重点显著不同。

### 5.1 AWS：配额可观测性 + 标签级限制 + 原生直方图计量优惠

Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus（AMP）基于 Cortex 构建，查询通过 PromQL（[Logz.io, 2023](https://logz.io/blog/comparing-prometheus-managed-services)）。AWS 在治理能力上最为系统化：

- **服务配额与 CloudWatch 用量指标**：AMP 提供 `IngestionRate`（每秒摄入样本数）、`ActiveSeries`（当前活跃序列数）、`DiscardedSamples`（因约束被丢弃的样本数）、`QueryMetricsTPS`、`RuleEvaluations` 等指标，支持通过 CloudWatch 告警在触及限制前预警；AWS Service Quotas 可一键查看已应用配额并申请提升（[AWS Docs, AMP quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prometheus/latest/userguide/AMP_quotas.html)）。
- **标签级活跃序列限制（label-based active series limits）**：允许按指标生产者（应用、服务、团队）设置特定上限，精确控制高基数摄入与成本——这是三大云厂商中独有的细分治理能力（[AWS Cloud Operations Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/optimizing-metrics-ingestion-with-amazon-managed-service-for-prometheus)）。
- **原生直方图计量优惠**：每个已填充桶（非零观测）仅计为 **0.25 个指标样本**，空桶不计费——直接降低了直方图工作负载的流失率成本（[AWS Pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/prometheus/pricing)）。

AMP 的已知短板是"纯指标"定位：需要单独购买 Amazon Managed Grafana 做可视化、CloudWatch Logs 收日志、X-Ray 收追踪，生产事故排障时需在多个控制台间切换，拖慢关联分析（[Logz.io, 2023](https://logz.io/blog/comparing-prometheus-managed-services)；[CubeAPM, 2026](https://cubeapm.com/blog/amazon-managed-service-prometheus-pricing-review)）。成本方面，AWS 自有定价示例显示 10 节点集群每月约 $81.75，50 节点约 $405（[CubeAPM, 2026](https://cubeapm.com/blog/amazon-managed-service-prometheus-pricing-review)）。

### 5.2 Google Cloud：Monarch 全局架构 + 24 个月长保留

Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus（GMP）构建在 Monarch——Google 内部用于监控自身服务的同一全球分布式数据存储之上（[Google Cloud Docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/managed-prometheus)）。其核心差异化能力：

- **全局查询**：支持跨项目、多云与混合云环境的 PromQL 查询，无需联邦即可对区域化数据做全局查询（[Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/managed-prometheus)）；
- **默认两年保留**：托管服务默认包含 24 个月指标保留期，无需自建长期存储（[Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/managed-prometheus)；[Logz.io, 2023](https://logz.io/blog/comparing-prometheus-managed-services)）；
- **成本控制机制**：导出指标过滤器、稀疏直方图减免费用、长采样周期费率递减、支持仅发送本地预聚合数据；可通过 Cloud Monitoring 按指标名与 namespace 归因摄入成本（[Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/managed-prometheus)）。

GMP 的定价为每百万样本 $0.060 起（0–500 亿样本区间），后续阶梯降至 $0.048、$0.036、$0.024（[Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/managed-prometheus)）。与 AWS 类似，GMP 也存在工具碎片化问题：Cloud Monitoring、Cloud Logging 与 GMP 分属不同界面，跨数据类型关联分析困难（[Logz.io, 2023](https://logz.io/blog/comparing-prometheus-managed-services)）。

### 5.3 Azure：混合云聚合 + 18 个月零成本保留

Azure Monitor 托管 Prometheus 使用 **Azure Monitor 工作区** 作为存储后端（[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/metrics/prometheus-metrics-overview)）。其显著特点：

- **多云一致性**：通过 Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes 与 Prometheus remote write，可聚合 AWS EKS 与 GCP GKE 集群的指标，使用同一套 Container insights 与 Managed Grafana 工具链实现跨云监控体验（[Microsoft Learn, multicloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/best-practices-multicloud)）；
- **18 个月数据保留且存储不额外收费**，定价仅基于摄入与查询（[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/metrics/prometheus-metrics-overview)）；
- **与自管理 Prometheus 集成**：支持通过 remote_write 将自建 Prometheus 数据发送至 Azure Monitor 工作区，作为迁移过渡或长期混合方案（[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/metrics/prometheus-metrics-overview)）。

### 5.4 三方能力对比总表

| 能力维度 | AWS AMP | GCP GMP | Azure Monitor |
|---------|---------|---------|---------------|
| 存储后端 | Cortex | Monarch | Azure Monitor 工作区 |
| 默认/最大保留期 | 按存储计费（默认无统一长保留） | 24 个月默认 | 18 个月，存储免费 |
| 全局/跨项目查询 | 不支持（需自行聚合） | 支持（跨项目/多云） | 支持（经 Arc + remote write） |
| 高基数治理特有功能 | 标签级活跃序列限制、CloudWatch 配额指标 | 导出过滤器、稀疏直方图减免 | 无公开的标签级限制 |
| 原生直方图 | 支持，填充桶按 0.25 样本计费 | 支持，稀疏直方图有减免 | 支持 |
| 计价基准 | 样本摄入分级 + 存储 + 查询样本 | 每百万样本 $0.060 起 | 摄入 + 查询样本 |
| 已知短板 | 纯指标，工具碎片化 | 工具碎片化 | 文档与功能成熟度参差 |

## 6. 结论与建议

基于上述分析，本报告形成以下判断：

**第一，高流失率治理必须前置到抓取阶段。** 所有有效的修复手段都作用于序列创建点——重标记、录制规则、抓取限制和原生直方图。查询端的优化（如 topk）只提升仪表盘速度，不缩减 TSDB 体积（[Last9, 2023](https://last9.io/blog/how-to-manage-high-cardinality-metrics-in-prometheus)）。

**第二，原生直方图是当前最具成本效益的结构性修复，但需要主动迁移。** 它不能自动转换既有直方图，也无法解决无界标签问题（[Logz.io, 2026](https://logz.io/blog/prometheus-metrics-native-histograms)）。将其部署在标签治理之上，才能同时解决"桶爆炸"与"标签爆炸"两个维度。

**第三，架构选型应遵循"Mimir 优先、Thanos 次之"的原则。** 新部署选择 Mimir 以获得集中式多租户能力；既有 Prometheus 舰队需要全局查询与长期保留时引入 Thanos；同时必须认识到 Thanos 对高基数问题无解（[Bigyan Raj Dahal](https://www.bigyanrajdahal.com/blog/when-to-use-mimir-cortex-thanos)；[Oodle AI Blog](https://blog.oodle.ai/scaling-prometheus-from-single-node-to-enterprise-grade-observability)）。

**第四，云厂商方案的核心差异在于"治理深度"而非"托管本身"。** AWS AMP 凭借标签级活跃序列限制与 CloudWatch 配额指标，提供了最细粒度的流失率治理能力；GCP GMP 凭借 Monarch 全局架构与 24 个月默认保留，在规模与全局查询上占优；Azure 则以多云聚合和 18 个月零成本保留见长。对于已深度绑定单一云厂商的团队，应优先选择该厂商的托管服务并将内置治理能力纳入告警体系；对于多云团队，Azure Arc 或 GCP 的跨项目查询是可行的统一入口。任何云厂商方案都无法替代应用侧的标签纪律——这是所有结论的共同前提。
